This drillhole was terminated within variably brecciated and minor haematite-altered (after disseminated magnetite) granite and microgranite that bear superficial similarity to the Olympic Dam deposit host granite. However, no significant downhole sample assay values were returned, the reported copper contents being less than 300 ppm. Following the interpretation of the new geophysical data, further exploratory/stratigraphic drilling was undertaken. Vertical diamond drillhole SGD1 was completed to TD 774 m at a site located ~22 km north-east of Olympic Dam. Basement was reached at 414 m depth, below which the hole penetrated a sequence of basic volcanic rocks containing minor chalcopyrite mineralisation. A second vertical diamond drillhole in the Phillips Ridge area, PD2, was completed to TD 436 m. Basement was encountered at 304 m depth, and consisted of unmineralised, coarse-grained biotite granite.

abstract: Brownfields copper exploration undertaken by WMC in the Todds Dam area, located about 17 km west-northwest of the Olympic Dam discovery, initially consisted of the acquisition of gravity and ground magnetic traverses across a poorly expressed regional gravity anomaly which it was hoped might be a continuation of the Olympic Dam coincident magnetic and gravity geophysical feature. Stratigraphic diamond drillhole TOD1 was spudded in early June 1977 within EL 279, close to the western boundary of the adjoining Arcoona EL 190/ EL 344, in order to test a prominent ground  magnetic anomaly, and after percussion precollar drilling to 119.2 m depth, was diamond cored vertically to TD 630 m during June-August 1977. After passing through a sequence consisting of Andamooka Limestone, Tregolana Shale and ? Nuccaleena Formation, the drillhole entered altered basement consisting of strongly deformed, intensely magnetic and very dense predominantly magnetite-chlorite rocks, and was continued for 97 m down into it. The penetrated basement is pervasively brecciated and carbonate-veined, and besides being mineralogically very rich in magnetite (average 15-20%), is also rich in magnesium - bearing minerals including serpentine, talc, tremolite, chlorite and dolomite. However, it was found to have a surprisingly low nickel content (average 40-50 ppm Ni), which was confirmed by repeat assaying of the drill core, and therefore, rather than indicating an expected ultramafic igneous precursor, the composition appeared enigmatically to have been derived from possible orthopyroxenites. However, some further geochemical analyses of these rocks suggested that they do not have alkaline igneous affinities, since they contain low levels of rare earths, niobium, phosphorus, vanadium and titanium, so then it was surmised that they may represent metamorphosed dolomitic sediments. A best mineralised intercept of 1450 ppm Cu, 1320 ppm Zn, 360 ppm Co, 320 ppm Pb and 120 ppm Ni was obtained over the cored depth interval 582-584 m in the aforesaid basement rocks. Elevated uranium values ranging between 8 to 18 ppm U were also recorded over a 40 m width of this section of the hole. Within the overlying basal ? Nuccaleena Formation, minor visible bornite and chalcopyrite occupying fracture cavities were logged between 522 and 531 m depth.  In view of the unusual basement lithology encountered in TOD1, WMC decided that the direction of future work on the subject tenement area would be dependent on drilling results to be realised at targets then being tested elsewhere on the project acreage. Additional ground geophysical survey traverses were commenced to the south of the original Todds Dam prospect grid, while part of the original grid was re-levelled to refine the gravity interpretation.   As reported in an annual exploration review document enclosed within the subject Envelope, for the Stuart Shelf Project combined tenement areas, 15 high priority geophysical targets have to date been identified by WMC which possess similar character to the geophysical signature of the Olympic Dam copper-uranium deposit discovered in November 1976. As of February 1978, nine of these targets have each been tested with a single stratigraphic/exploratory drillhole. Most of these drillholes revealed encouraging results with respect to basement mineralisation and geological setting, and warrant follow-up drilling.

The survey results indicated that the majority of the licence east of the Torrens Hinge Zone is underlain by very deep magnetic basement, which gave little encouragement for WMC's intent to carry out exploratory drilling. Further work was postponed until July 1978, after the company had completed drilling at West Well prospect on its adjoining EL 404 to the south. A post-drill reinterpretation of the geophysical data in the light of the Adelaidean strata encountered down to TD 762.1 m in hole WWD1, which did not reach basement, but was stopped in Bayley Range Siltstone (Woomera/Tregolana Shale equivalent) suggested that the basement there could lie deeper than 2 km. This adverse finding implied that only the western part of EL 292 might be of further interest. It was decided to await the outcome of other diamond drilling being conducted at Bills Lookout prospect on EL 269 before doing any more detailed ground geophysical work to try to delineate the Lake Arthur magnetic anomaly.

abstract: Exploration undertaken by Western Mining Corp. in a search for possible economic Mount Gunson - type stratiform copper mineralisation that could have formed within a sequence of buried Adelaidean metasediments of the eastern Stuart Shelf which in part subcrop on EL 293, initially comprised ground geophysical surveys aimed at delineating some interpreted regional magnetic and gravity anomalies situated over central Lake Torrens near Murdie Island. 350 line km of ground magnetic and gravity traverses were acquired during February-May 1978, after commencement of the work had been delayed by the process of obtaining balloon-tyred, lightweight 3-wheeled motorcycles suitable for safely accessing the soft surface of the salt lake. abstract: During exploration carried out in an area located approximately 60 km south-west of Anna Creek, Newmont targeted Zambian Copperbelt - style mineralisation similar to perceived equivalents of the then newly discovered and poorly understood Olympic Dam deposit. Newmont had earlier noted an alignment of known Stuart Shelf copper deposits sub-parallel to the Torrens Hinge Zone, near or coincident with basement highs, and often associated with positive magnetic or gravity anomalies.  Within a package of eight tenements that it has lately secured on ground lying north-west of Olympic Dam, which it is exploring in a 50:50 joint venture with BHP subsidiary Dampier Mining Co., Newmont investigated the Coolawarra gravity anomaly situated 25 km north-east of Mount Woods by acquiring ground magnetic and gravity surveys, followed by the drilling of 2 vertical percussion / diamond cored, rotary mud precollared stratigraphic holes designed to test geophysical targets on the northern flank of this anomaly. The intent was to check whether inferred prospective Upper Proterozoic metasediments, that elsewhere on the Stuart Shelf occur above the Roopena Volcanics, are present beneath the Mesozoic and Permian cover to the Boorthanna Trough.  Hole SR2 encountered foliated quartz-biotite-feldspar-garnet gneiss from 119.6 -130 m depth. Hole SR3 was abandoned in Mesozoic sediments at TD 380 m.  Since the target Adelaidean metasedimentary section was not encountered by the drilling, and because the younger cover around the Coolawarra basement high appeared in general to be more than 380 m deep, and a similar situation was thought to apply at other mapped magnetic and gravity anomalies in the Birthday Hill area, a decision was made to discontinue work there.

abstract: Continuing exploration in the Woomera area has included the acquisition of a ground magnetic and gravity survey over the Buller Dam anomaly, which lies on the western flank of the Acropolis aeromagnetic anomaly, and this work confirmed that the former lies on the flank of both the magnetic and gravity regional anomalies. A 304 m percussion precollared, vertical NQ/BQ diamond drillhole PPR5/SAP1 that was subsequently drilled at a location 700 m west of Buller Dam during September-October 1979 was terminated within Pandurra Formation at 1369.3 m depth. Magnetic susceptibility and density measurements were made on drill core samples of the various stratigraphic units intersected.  A trial airborne magnetic / radiometric survey was flown along two orthogonal traverses over the Portulacca Ridge and Eucolo gravity anomalies in November 1980.  In December 1980, a 700 station gravity survey was acquired over the Eucolo regional gravity anomaly, and it revealed a NNW trending, 5 mGal amplitude ridge - shaped gravity high anomaly, 3 km wide and 8 km long.  Modelling of these surveys' data suggested that the source depth of the gravity anomaly lies at 1000 m, and that of the magnetic anomaly at 300 m, the latter thus possibly representing a magnetic horizon within the Gawler Range Volcanics, with denser basement present below the volcanic rocks.  No drilling has yet been carried out on this anomaly.  Most of EL 933, except for a small area around the Portulacca Ridge and Buller Dam Grid, was relinquished in August 1982.

abstract: An area of the southern Stuart Shelf, with untested potential for hosting possible stratiform base metal deposits within a probable concealed Early Proterozoic sedimentary basin embayment, was explored by BP as part of their regional mineral evaluation of that province.  A series of 12 percussion stratigraphic/exploratory holes (total 1410 m) plus one diamond hole (30.35 m) were drilled to find the distribution of the preserved erosional top surface of the Pandurra Formation. Radiometric logging of drillholes proved a valuable tool for subsurface correlation of the surrounding stratigraphic units, enabling a number of conclusions to be made about their past deposition, relations to intrusive igneous bodies, and history of erosion or preservation.  Only sparse copper mineralisation (malachite, chalcopyrite) was encountered downhole.  Two aeromagnetic anomalies were recovered by ground magnetic surveys, but their attributes for indicating possible Olympic Dam type mineralisation in the deeper, pre-Pandurra basement were considered unlikely to match reality.

abstract: Basal Neoproterozoic Tapley Hill Formation - hosted stratiform copper was targeted primarily in this exploration programme, which consisted of reconnaissance deep percussion drilling (17 holes for a total advance of 4167 m) on the centres of aeromagnetic highs after they had been further delineated by ground magnetometry. One of the percussion holes (PIL3) was deepened with a 140.4 m diamond tail (DDH SAI-1) to investigate the potential for Olympic Dam - type mineralisation in the pre-Pandurra basement. All drillholes were radiometrically logged for stratigraphic correlation purposes. Base metal potential in the upper Tapley Hill sequence is considered high, with elevated background zinc levels, although only minor Pb-Zn mineralisation was intersected. No Tapley Hill Formation is present on the western side of Lake Macfarlane. The stratigraphy, sedimentary geology and distribution of the Pandurra Formation was further unravelled, and also its contact relationships to older Gairdner Dolerite dykes and the Gawler Range Volcanics, which were penetrated by a few of the drillholes.  The drilling carried out in the south-western part of EL 301 has disclosed a buried sequence of Pandurra Formation sedimentary rocks that are generally greater than 300 m in thickness, and which shallow to the west.  The sequence is lithologically remarkably similar going from hole to hole, and the formation can be subdivided into several distinct members of regional extent.  No significant mineralisation was seen either within the Pandurra interval or at its basal unconformable contact with the Gawler Range Volcanics. There are no favourable lithotypes present in the basal Pandurra in the area so far drilled, which might host Zambian Copperbelt - type base metal deposits.  Also, no prominent magnetic or gravity anomalies exist in this south-western area which might indicate Olympic Dam style mineralised basement bodies.  Accordingly, the south-western portion of the licence area will be relinquished when tenure is renewed in early 1979.

name: mesac5892
title: Danae Hill (part of the Stuart Range Joint Venture Project). Progress reports and final report to licence full surrender, for the period 30/3/1977 to 31/7/1978.
notes:
Geographic Locality: Danae Hill;Millers Creek Station;Margaret Creek;Woomera Prohibited Area;1977 Danae Hill Gravity Survey
Doc No: Env 03017
Drillhole: SR1;(14114);SR5;(137871);SR16;(137872)
abstract: Following the first public announcement on 18/11/1976 by Western Mining Corp. of its giant Olympic Dam copper, gold and uranium discovery on Roxby Downs Station, Newmont Pty Ltd began a detailed assessment of the Stuart Shelf region of South Australia. Although the latter company did not yet know the nature of the mineralisation or controlling host strata at Olympic Dam, it swiftly made application to the SA Department of Mines for the grant of exploration licences over available ground located north-west of Olympic Dam, selecting areas occupying a trend that lay to the east of the Torrens Hinge Zone (THZ). The subject Danae Hill area was chosen because it covers a sharp magnetic anomaly which is coincident with an isolated gravity anomaly. Both geophysical features lie on the south-eastern flank of the Mount Woods basement high, on a culmination between the Boorthanna and Lake Phillipson Troughs, but locally there are no crystalline basement outcrops. Newmont entered into a 50:50 joint venture partnership with BHP subsidiary Dampier Mining Co. early in 1977, and EL 304 was granted to both companies in March along with two other Exploration Licences covering adjoining ground in the Twins (Outstation) and Coolawarra areas which looked to have a similar geophysical character, and which lay to the west of a linear crustal feature that appeared to link major copper deposits further south (Olympic Dam, Mount Gunson and Moonta-Wallaroo). Within the Newmont-Dampier exploration project area, the target sought was of Olympic Dam type, i.e. large tonnage, low grade primary Cu-U mineralisation occurring in or near to a crystalline basement host.  Field activities commenced in April 1977 with the pegging of a prospect grid consisting of three 10 km long lines spaced 2.5 km apart. Ground magnetic survey readings were made at 250 m intervals along the grid traverses, followed in early June 1977 by a gravity survey of 72 stations read at 500 m intervals on the grid. The data from these surveys was interpreted and a preferred drill site located, in the absence of reliable density data about the local stratigraphic profile, near the peak of the gravity anomaly, was picked by Newmont's chief geophysicist for conducting an initial stratigraphic test. The intent was to drill to 350-400 m depth to try to penetrate possible Upper Proterozoic strata, i.e. metasediments or granitic breccias, that might contain geochemical vectors to mineralisation.  Drilling was begun in early July 1977, when vertical hole SR1 was first rotary percussion drilled and then (from 96 m depth) NQ diamond cored to 158 m depth, ending in epidote amphibolite. Another vertical hole, SR5, was drilled in October at a site 1 km north-east of SR1, in an attempt to obtain a deeper penetration of basement, and it was completed at 199.0 m depth after encountering similar epidote amphibolite rock at 195.55 m. Coring here started at 181 .5 m depth. Four selected drill core samples of permeable rock material taken from 10-15 cm intervals surrounding the impervious Cretaceous sediment / basement amphibolite unconformity in hole SR1 were sent for laboratory emission spectroscopic analysis, to determine whether meteoric waters circulating in this zone are carrying any trace metal pathfinder elements. No assay values of interest were reported. All of the drill cuttings and cores from both holes were scanned using a hand-held gamma ray spectrometer, but readings averaged only 1-4 counts per second of combined U/Th radiation. Two samples of the basement amphibolite encountered in the bottom of holes SR1 and SR5 were sent to a petrological consultant for examination. He considered the rocks to be comparable retrograde metamorphosed basic igneous rocks, the protolith probably being a quartz dolerite. He said that the rocks have none of the characteristics of metasediments. To assist with the interpretation of the gravity results, 14 percussion chip and drill core samples from hole SR1 were sent to Amdel for bulk density determination. In late December 1977, a third vertical stratigraphic hole, SR16, was rotary percussion precollared to 76 m depth at a location towards the north-east, as it was intended to probe further down the interpreted flank of the basement structural high, in an attempt to obtain a deeper basement intercept, hopefully of favourable Adelaidean metasedimentary strata. There followed a delay during the first quarter of 1978, as no diamond drill rig was available to continue this hole. It was re-entered in May and was NQ/BQ cored to a total depth of 241.0 m, ending within unmineralised epidote amphibolite that is more feldspathic than the rocks penetrated at the bottom of SR1 and SR5. This probably less magnetic rock type was penetrated at a depth of 227.13 m, beneath partly carbonaceous shales and massive diamictite beds. Its position revealed that at Danae Hill the basement unconformity dips almost flatly towards the north-east beneath about 200 m thickness of Mesozoic cover.

abstract: Concerted exploration for possible stratiform Mount Gunson type or epithermal Olympic Dam type base metal deposits, on the south-eastern edge of the Stuart Shelf near Port Pirie, was begun by North Broken Hill Ltd in response to the public release by Western Mining Corp. of initial geological information about its recent giant orebody discovery on Roxby Downs Station.  NBH targeted a large regional aeromagnetic high at Wandearah with detailed ground gravity and ground magnetic surveys, which disclosed a number of likely gravity and magnetic sources in the previously untested deep metasedimentary sequence of Adelaidean age.  These inferred iron-rich anomalies were progressively diamond drilled by NBH in 15 stratigraphic/exploratory core holes totalling 6657.18 m. Widespread, disseminated low grade base metal sulphide, ilmenite - haematite - molybdenite and uranium oxide mineralisation was found over the south-western portion of a 25 km x 17 km area at many stratigraphic levels within a strongly block-faulted post - Pandurra Formation sequence, occurring typically within carbonate veins or the matrix quartzite of conglomeratic and fault-brecciated sediments, or in reduced graphitic-argillaceous shale facies proximal to redbed units and to isolated, altered acid-intermediate and trachybasalt interbeds of the Beda Volcanics.  Examples of trace to minor chalcocite - chalcopyrite - pyrite - bearing intersections include 25.6 m of 0.16% Cu below 226.1 m depth in conglomerates in hole PP2, and 0.72% Cu over 7.25 m in hole PP5, the latter interval entraining 2.7 m @ 1.53% Cu below 297.8 m.  Minor uranium mineralisation up to 250 ppm U was present in grey siltstones below the Sturt Tillite in drillhole PP3, and this hole also showed anomalous cobalt in zones of high copper assays, plus scattered gold values of about 0.3 g/t Au.  Trace to minor galena and sphalerite were intersected near the base of the Tapley Hill Formation in drillhole PP4 and in several subsequent nearby holes.  In the light of these results, Aquitaine Australia Minerals entered into a 40% joint venture with NBH in the second half of 1978. The programme of drilling is yielding encouraging results, both in terms of stratigraphic discoveries and in exploration model formulation, and will be continued.

abstract: Continuing exploration for possible buried Mount Gunson and Olympic Dam type copper deposits, or other stratabound base metal occurrences within shelfal facies of Adelaidean sediments or in the pre-Adelaidean Wandearah Formation Carpentarian age metasediments that subcrop over an area extending southwards from Port Germein to the Broughton River delta, has centred on evaluation of coincident aeromagnetic / gravity anomalies, including a number generated from new ground magnetic and gravity traverses.  Diamond drilling (4 holes in this period : thus making overall 20 holes totalling 9208.45 m) has, however, encountered only traces of galena and weak, disseminated copper sulphide mineralisation in the lower Sturtian interval rocks. The strong combined magnetic/gravity high at Wandearah West was shown to arise from a structural uplift in the Carpentarian basement, it having within it a pronounced haematitic iron enrichment in the metasiltstones drilled, to the extent that they can essentially be regarded as iron formations.  Following the licence farm-in of Aquitaine Minerals in June 1979, additional drill targets were sought by acquiring detailed ground magnetic and gravity surveys.  A 1.7 mGal residual gravity anomaly centred 4 km north-west of Port Germein was investigated by DDH PP20, after a 29-station gravity appraisal on a 400 m x 400 m grid had been completed to define its closure.  The drillhole was terminated at a total depth of 356 m in Adelaidean Brachina Formation shales and siltstones containing minor chalcopyrite, without finding any obvious explanation for the gravity anomaly. 5 auger and air-drilled percussion holes totalling 226 m were put down near the south-eastern corner of the licence area to search for economic Tertiary lignite, thin seams of which had earlier been disclosed by DDH PP6, but this drilling too had no success.

abstract: Ongoing exploration for possible Mount Gunson - type base metal occurrences has included percussion drilling on a metal ratio geochemical anomaly identified proximal to inferred buried Beda Volcanics at Charlinga (10 holes totalling 1218 m), plus the compilation variously of structure contours for the pre- Tapley Hill Formation erosion surface, of isopach maps (Tapley Hill Formation, Willochra Subgroup equivalent, Yudnapinna Beds, Whyalla Sandstone), and of a pre- Tapley Hill Formation subcrop map. The drilling results overall were disappointing, although a best assay value of 380 ppm Cu was obtained from pyritic Pandurra Formation quartzite in hole BK22.  A computer-based statistical study of all past drillhole sample geochemistry was used to compile maps that show stratabound copper and lead distribution (for the Cainozoic, Whyalla Sandstone, Yudnapinna Beds, Tapley Hill Formation, Pandurra Formation and these combined stratigraphic intervals).  A photogeological study of structural elements in the Charlinga area has been commissioned from Hunting Geology and Geophysics, and had neared completion at the time of licence renewal.  A series of 1:100,000 scale major data group summary maps will shortly be prepared to assist in locating possible future drilling targets.

abstract: In a search for possible economic repetitions of Cattlegrid and MG14 - style copper sulphide mineralisation, or for any buried analogues to Western Mining Corp.'s recently discovered copper deposits on Roxby Downs Station, ongoing exploratory work undertaken in the Mount Gunson area has included:  - stepout percussion drilling at Cattlegrid to look for orebody extensions;  - deep stratigraphic percussion drilling at MG11, Elizabeth Creek, Wirrapa and Lake Dutton;  - a deep stratigraphic test, by diamond drilling, of the strongly dipolar aeromagnetic anomaly 'A' located 5 km north of Lucas Hill, sourced by an interpreted flat-lying tabular body (vertical DDH LH1 to TD 788 m, including 232 m RC precollared, drilled during February-April 1978). This drillhole failed to reach pre-Adelaidean basement;  - continuing interpretations of regional Landsat, gravity and aeromagnetic data;  - acquisition and processing of a 2300 line km low level aeromagnetic survey, flown by Geoex Pty Ltd during August 1978 at 300 m flight line spacing and 100 m mean terrain clearance;  - follow-up of selected geochemical and geophysical anomalies by percussion drilling and ground magnetic and gravity surveys;  - the conduct of trial IP surveys aimed at mapping the limits of the Tapley Hill Formation and possibly locating any significant accumulations of sulphide mineralisation within this unit;  - the conduct of a trial seismic reflection survey aimed at mapping unconformities bounding the Tapley Hill Formation, and delineating the geometry of block fault structures that might have controlled its deposition and facies;  - detailed petrographic studies of drill core samples of the 'McLeay Beds', Tapley Hill Formation and Pandurra Formation;   - compilation of bedrock lithology, structure contour (Hiatus 3, pre- and post- Tapley Hill Formation erosion surfaces) and isopach maps (Tapley Hill Formation, Yudnapinna Beds, Yudnapinna Beds / Whyalla Sandstone, Whyalla Sandstone and Tregolana Shale); and  - resampling of drill cuttings for previously unattempted assays, and their relogging.  Percussion drilling undertaken late in 1977 at the South Windabout prospect, 6 km away from Cattlegrid, gave encouraging results when 3 of 13 holes encountered >1% Cu over thicknesses of up to 5 m at the top of the Tapley Hill Formation. Another single hole drilled on the Cattlegrid Extension grid at this time also had >2% Cu over 1 m. However, DDH LW66 completed in September 1978 returned the best intercept so far made in the brownfields exploration programme, when drill core cut in the upper Tapley Hill Formation between 46 and 48 m depth assayed 4.18% Cu and 32 g/t Ag. The predominantly chalcocite mineralisation has a supergene type, fracture-filling habit, and lies within an oxidised shale sequence.

name: mesac5118
title: The Twins (part of the Stuart Range Joint Venture Project). Progress reports and final report to licence full surrender, for the period 30/3/1977 to 31/7/1978.
notes:
Geographic Locality: McDouall Peak Station;The Twins Station;Stuart Highway;Woomera Prohibited Area;1977 McDouall Peak Gravity Survey;1977 Hawks Nest Gravity Survey;1978 Mirikata Gravity Survey
Doc No: Env 03031
Drillhole: SR7;(9706);SR9;(9709);SR15;(9710)
abstract: Following the first public announcement on 18/11/1976 by Western Mining Corp. of its giant Olympic Dam copper, gold and uranium discovery on Roxby Downs Station, Newmont Pty Ltd began a detailed assessment of the Stuart Shelf region of South Australia. Although the latter company did not yet know the nature of the mineralisation or controlling host strata at Olympic Dam, it swiftly made application to the SA Department of Mines for the grant of exploration licences over available ground located north-west of Olympic Dam, selecting areas occupying a trend that lay to the east of the Torrens Hinge Zone (THZ). The subject Margaret Creek area was chosen because it covered coincident broad regional gravity and magnetic anomalies that are situated close to the southern edge of the Phillipson Trough. Newmont entered into a 50:50 joint venture partnership with BHP subsidiary Dampier Mining Co. early in 1977, and EL 305 was granted to both companies in March along with two other Exploration Licences covering adjoining ground in the Danae Hill and Coolawarra areas which looked to have a similar geophysical character, and which lay to the west of a linear crustal feature that appeared to link major copper deposits further south (Olympic Dam, Mount Gunson and Moonta-Wallaroo). Within the Newmont-Dampier exploration project area, the target sought was of Olympic Dam type, i.e. large tonnage, low grade primary Cu-U mineralisation occurring in or near to a crystalline basement host.  Initial field activities commenced in April 1977, with the acquisition of detailed ground magnetic and gravity surveys over the McDouall Peak gravity anomaly in the west of EL 305. A prospect grid was surveyed there and reconnaissance hand-held magnetometer readings were taken at 250 m intervals along three 10 km long principal traverses. Solo Geophysics were contracted during July 1977 to take gravity readings at 250 m x 2000 m station spacing (140 readings collected). Interpretation of the resulting magnetic and gravity data indicated that crystalline basement occurs at shallow depth, so it was decided not to drill test this anomaly.  Attention shifted to the Hawks Nest gravity anomaly situated 24 km to the SSE. Ground magnetic surveying conducted there by Newmont in September 1977 along two 8 km long traverses spaced 2.5 km apart defined a sharp 1400 gamma peak coinciding with the gravity high, and this was thought to reflect banded iron formation units present in the Cleve Metamorphics at this locality, because such rocks outcrop to the west of the grid. To better define the anomaly and provide a selection of drill sites, Solo Geophysics read 76 gravity stations at Hawks Nest, also at 250 m station intervals, during the month.  Exploratory/stratigraphic percussion hole SR7 was drilled vertically at Hawks Nest to a total depth of 67.2 m during October 1977. The hole was stopped within fresh chloritic schist, after passing through a weathered basement section that probably extends from ~35 m to 65.7 m depth. A second hole, SR9, also sited on the flank of the Hawks Nest anomaly, was drilled to 71.4 m total depth during November 1977. It bottomed in a lithic plagioclase-quartz wacke having a chlorite-sericite matrix. This was thought to be part of a ?Cretaceous pebble horizon overlying basement. A third stratigraphic drillhole at Hawks Nest, SR15, was afterwards precollared to 85.8 m depth at a site 7 km to the west-northwest of SR9. It encountered a hard, fine grained pale greenish-brown quartzite at 84.2 m, which was correlated with the unit at the base of SR9 as a downdip facies equivalent. Newmont decided to return to hole SR9 and deepen it with a diamond cored tail to obtain samples of the underlying basement, to help determine if any prospective Proterozoic rocks are present at Hawks Nest. This extension drilling at SR9 took place in December 1977, with 19.1 m of coring done down to 90.5 m depth. The entire core lithology consists of a slightly pyritic, metamorphosed coarse grained litharkosic wacke, in which the pebbles have been stretched along the foliation. Newmont considered this rock to be part of the Cleve Metamorphics. The diamond rig was shifted back to SR15 to deepen it also, with an additional 25.7 m of coring completed to TD 111.5 m. This showed that the ?Cretaceous or ?Permian sandstone sequence there continues to 104.3 m depth, before transitioning into a dark grey, medium grained arkosic wacke similar to the rock types seen at the bottom of SR9. The rock contains 2-3% disseminated pyrite as grains averaging ~1 mm diameter. Laboratory semi-quantitative emission spectroscopic chemical analyses were made of selected core samples collected at 10 cm intervals from the lower part of both drillholes, but the results were uninteresting, apart from slightly anomalous lead (highest values 100 ppm and 300 ppm Pb) in samples from the interval 69.5-89.5 m in hole SR9. All of the drill cuttings and cores from the three exploratory holes were scanned using a hand-held gamma ray spectrometer, but readings averaged only 1-2 counts per second of combined U/Th radiation.  Because the Hawks Nest anomaly appeared to be underlain at shallow depth by the Cleve Metamorphics, the JV partners decided that further exploration there was not warranted. However, a recent re-evaluation of regional geophysical anomalies within the licence area had identified a distinct circular aeromagnetic anomaly situated 5 km north-northeast from the Mirikata Tracking Station, which it was thought could have exploration potential. Consequently, application was made to SADME for an extension of tenure period for six months, from March to September 1978, to allow for making an investigation of this feature.  Ground magnetic readings and a detailed gravity survey of 126 stations were acquired on it during April 1978, over a 250 m x 2500 m grid of three principal lines pegged as an extension of the McDouall Peak grid. The magnetic anomaly appeared to be caused by two sources - a low-order NW trending anomaly possibly, caused by BIF or a basic dyke, and an unusually sharp 2000 gamma anomaly crossing this at right angles. A low order gravity trend was defined coinciding with the NW trending magnetic anomaly, but the NE trending magnetic anomaly had no gravity expression, and was discounted as a target.  Subsequent considerations of this feature's geophysical character and of the licence's overall prospectivity downgraded both when, in the light of the wider drilling results that they had so far obtained, the partners concluded that Proterozoic basement was unlikely to exist there, nor within the JV's other tenements located too far west of the Torrens Hinge Zone and the major tectonic lineament belt. Therefore tenure of EL 305 was surrendered during July 1978.

abstract: Exploration for possible Olympic Dam type base metal sulphide deposits within the pre-Adelaidean basement underlying an area 100 km north-east of Kingoonya initially included making over 100 rock unit density and magnetic susceptibility measurements on stored drill cores from three prior deep boreholes, plus the acquisition and processing of a detailed 620 line km airborne magnetic and radiometric survey, and then ground magnetic and gravity follow-up of 10 aeromagnetic anomalies. It was concluded that most of the local geophysical anomalies are related to northwest-trending dykes. Vertical percussion drillhole CLK1, put down approximately 10 km south-west of Millers Creek Homestead to test both a weak magnetic anomaly and the associated strata, was abandoned at 152 m depth in ?Permian clay. abstract: As part of a regional search for possible buried Olympic Dam type, Middle Proterozoic basement-hosted base and precious metal deposits, a prominent aeromagnetic anomaly located just to the east of Pinery Dam was delineated and its source modelled by data collected along ground magnetic and gravity survey traverses.  The model derived was of a steeply dipping source body, 3 km long and up to 800 m wide, elongated north-south and lying on the north-west flank of a broad gravity high.  DDH CD1 was drilled to 150 m depth to test these anomalies and to elucidate the local stratigraphy. Adelaidean age Stuart Shelf sediments were not intersected before reaching basement. The aeromagnetic anomaly originating from therein is attributed to an ilmenite-rich dolerite dyke which apparently intrudes the Gawler Range Volcanics.  Drill core sample assaying returned generally low trace metal values, and no significant mineralisation was recorded.

Drillhole Unit No: 6429 00812;6429 00258;6429 00260;6429 00259
abstract: Continuation by Aquitaine of its regional appraisal of the mineral potential in the Cambrian carbonate sequence on northern Yorke Peninsula, has recently involved them in acquiring and interpreting ground gravity and magnetic surveys, completing a programme of bedrock drilling to obtain bedrock geochemical samples, and drilling 2 deeper rotary/percussion holes through the target sequence, with one of these holes subsequently being extended into the Adelaidean section by diamond drilling, while a third stratigraphic hole was independently diamond drilled nearby, also aiming to test the Adelaidean. Vertical stratigraphic percussion drillholes SYP602 and SYM600 (total penetration 341.5 m) were designed to probe an interpreted flat-lying shelf of Cambrian deposition near Kainton that appears to be controlled by a north-east trending normal fault. Trace chalcopyrite seen in the lower part of the Kulpara Formation in both drillholes corresponded with a maximum assay of 1600 ppm Cu attained in SYM600. A re-interpretation of existing aeromagnetic data was carried out in late 1977 that defined an area of relatively shallow magnetic basement close to Kainton, of the order of 200 m deep.  This probable fault-bounded structure was further delineated in 1978 by 78 line km of gravity surveying (230 stations read) and by 210 line km of ground magnetics. To evaluate the base metal potential of likely mineralised Adelaidean rocks contained inside this structure, the previously mentioned diamond drilling was undertaken next. Vertical diamond drillhole SYM101 (TD 201 m) confirmed the existence of a shallow magnetic basement block, and demonstrated the complete absence of any Adelaidean clastic units beneath the Sturtian tillites. It penetrated 23.9 m of Tertiary-Quaternary sediments, 100 m of Kulpara Limestone, 12.2 m of Winulta Formation and 50.8 m of tillite. Minor traces of chalcopyrite were noted in the Kulpara and Winulta intervals. Drillhole SYM600 was deepened below 199.5 m with a 107.5 m long diamond tail (DDH SYM102), to investigate a possible Mount Gunson type Woocalla Dolomite section thought to underlie the Winulta Formation. The coring encountered a 122.2 m thick Sturtian tillitic sequence, underlain by 22.1 m of Emeroo Quartzite and 16.2+ m of Willamulka Volcanics, down to TD 307.5 m.  No copper mineralisation was found except for minor traces seen at the top of the Willamulka Volcanics. The shallow reconnaissance drag-bit drilling for bedrock geochemistry which was undertaken in the northern part of the licence near Kulpara (36 holes for 308 m) did not provide any encouragement for further work. However, in the southern part of the EL significant trace copper values were detected at the base of the Kulpara Formation in an area south of Melton (up to 350 ppm Cu and 210 ppm Pb) and in the ?Ramsay Limestone south-east of Dowlingville (up to 900 ppm Pb and 440 ppm Zn).  Problems with obtaining access onto land inhibited early follow-up to these results, and in view of the overall poor exploration success, a decision to surrender the licence was made in October 1978.

title: Mount Sandy (part of the Stuart Range Joint Venture Project). Progress reports and final report to licence expiry/full surrender, for the period 3/5/1977 to 2/5/1978.

abstract: Following the first public announcement on 18/11/1976 by Western Mining Corp. of its giant Olympic Dam copper, gold and uranium discovery on Roxby Downs Station, Newmont Pty Ltd began a detailed assessment of the Stuart Shelf region of South Australia. Although the latter company did not yet know the nature of the mineralisation or controlling host strata at Olympic Dam, it swiftly made application to the SA Department of Mines for the grant of exploration licences over available ground located north-west of Olympic Dam, selecting areas occupying a trend that lay to the east of the Torrens Hinge Zone (THZ). The subject Danae Hill area was chosen because it covers the south-western flank of the Mount Woods basement high where it slopes down into the east-west trending Lake Phillipson Trough. A coincident gravity/magnetic anomaly of interest lay near the central-eastern boundary of the licence area. Newmont entered into a 50:50 joint venture partnership with BHP subsidiary Dampier Mining Co. early in 1977, and EL 326 was granted to both companies in the middle of that year along with seven other Exploration Licences covering adjoining ground in the Anna Creek - Mount Woods region which looked to have a similar geophysical character, and which lay over a linear crustal feature that appeared to link major copper deposits further south (Olympic Dam, Mount Gunson and Moonta-Wallaroo). Within the Newmont-Dampier exploration project area, the target sought was of Olympic Dam type, i.e. large tonnage, low grade primary Cu-U mineralisation occurring in or near to a crystalline basement host.  Field activities commenced in late June 1977 with the pegging of a prospect reconnaissance grid consisting of three 10 km long lines spaced 2.5 km apart. Ground magnetic survey readings were made at 250 m intervals along the grid traverses, followed in late July 1977 by a gravity survey of 98 stations read at 250 m intervals on the grid. The data from these surveys were interpreted, and a preferred drill site, located, in the absence of reliable density data about the local stratigraphic profile, near the peak of the gravity anomaly, was picked by Newmont's chief geophysicist for conducting an initial stratigraphic test. The intent was to drill to 350-400 m depth to try to penetrate possible Upper Proterozoic strata, i.e. metasediments or granitic breccias, that might contain geochemical vectors to mineralisation.  Drilling began during October 1977, when hole SR4 was rotary percussion precollared to 81.5 m depth, before being continued with NQ diamond coring to a total depth of 102.5 m. This hole penetrated a foliated chlorite-garnet-quartz-feldspar gneiss at 83.0 m depth. Another drill site was selected 1.25 km to the south-east, and hole SR10 was precollared in early November to a depth of 55.4 m, whereupon drilling was stopped within a pebbly conglomerate similar to that intersected just above basement in the previous hole. At this point it was decided not to continue the hole by diamond coring. Later scintillometer scans of the recovered drill cuttings and core gave very low radioactivity responses (1-4 counts per second combined U/Th).  The drilling results showed that the trough structure indicated by geophysics did not exist. No other geophysical targets were evident. It was inferred by Newmont that Proterozoic strata are unlikely to exist at shallow depth on EL 326, and when viewed in the light of recent drilling results the JV had obtained on their Birthday Hill EL 303 to the north, the decision was made to surrender the subject licence.

title: Codna Hill (part of the Stuart Range Joint Venture Project). Progress reports to licence expiry/renewal, for the period 3/5/1977 to 2/5/1979.

abstract: Following the first public announcement on 18/11/1976 by Western Mining Corp. of its giant Olympic Dam copper, gold and uranium discovery on Roxby Downs Station, Newmont Pty Ltd began a detailed assessment of the Stuart Shelf region of South Australia. Although the latter company did not yet know the nature of the mineralisation or controlling host strata at Olympic Dam, it swiftly made application to the SA Department of Mines for the grant of exploration licences over available ground located north-west of Olympic Dam, selecting areas occupying a trend that lay to the east of the Torrens Hinge Zone (THZ). The subject Codna Hill area was chosen because it covered coincident broad regional gravity and magnetic anomalies that are situated close to the intersection of an east-northeast trending geophysical lineament and the THZ. Newmont entered into a 50:50 joint venture partnership with BHP subsidiary Dampier Mining Co. early in 1977, and EL 327 was granted to both companies in the middle of that year along with six other Exploration Licences covering adjoining ground in the Anna Creek - Mount Woods region which looked to have a similar geophysical character, and which lay over a linear crustal feature that appeared to link major copper deposits further south (Olympic Dam, Mount Gunson and Moonta-Wallaroo). Within the Newmont-Dampier exploration project area, the target sought was of Olympic Dam type, i.e. large tonnage, low grade primary Cu-U mineralisation occurring in or near to a crystalline basement host.  Initial field activities commenced in August 1977, with the acquisition of detailed ground magnetic and gravity surveys over regional geophysical anomalies, which in the case of EL 327 comprised the Mount Allalone gravity anomaly. A prospect grid was surveyed there and reconnaissance hand-held magnetometer readings were taken at 250 m intervals along three 8 km long traverses. No discrete magnetic highs were identified associated with these traverses. Solo Geophysics were contracted next to take gravity readings at 250 m x 250 m grid spacing over the Mount Allalone anomaly, and the resulting values from 116 stations defined a broad high. A preferred drill site was picked by Newmont's chief geophysicist for conducting an initial stratigraphic test.  Drilling was begun in early November 1977, when vertical rotary mud hole SR11 was carried to 103.9 m, at which depth the hole was abandoned due to sticking drill pipe. A second twin hole, SR12, commenced drilling close by immediately afterwards, but realising progress proved very  difficult, necessitating a change of drilling method and contractor. This hole took until May 1978 to reach a depth of 399.0 m, and was terminated there within inferred Permian strata. Diamond coring was conducted in SR12 (NQ and BQ respectively between 98.89-154.5 m and from that depth to hole TD), with reasonable core recoveries obtained throughout. Later scintillometer scans of the recovered drill core gave very low radioactivity responses (2-4 counts per second combined U/Th).  While the ground geophysical surveys and drilling were underway and during the months following, Newmont carried out office-based regional basin studies to inform its stratabound, African Copperbelt style epigenetic mineralisation model. Using stratigraphic data from water wells and other boreholes, it estimated that 500-600 m thickness of Recent to Palaeozoic cover sediments might exist at the Mount Allalone prospect. An in-house study of 1:100,000 scale aerial photomosaics and Landsat images was performed to map lineaments over a wide prospective belt running northward along the Torrens Hinge Zone from Moonta to the northern end of the Stuart Range Project acreage, and the aforementioned prominent NNW-trending lineament was clearly identified. Additional lineaments were also seen to pass through the Mount Allalone feature; a prominent ENE trending gravity/magnetic high, and a nearby subsidiary ERTS imaged lineament running parallel about 25 km west of the major Mount Gunson - Olympic Dam lineament zone.  Important stratigraphic drilling planned for adjacent Project licences, which would determine if deeper drilling should be attempted on EL 327, was delayed for nine months during 1978 by unseasonally wet weather in the SA Outback, but early in 1979 three deep diamond holes were begun from existing precollared sites on ELs 341 and 355, aiming to penetrate the as-yet still untested basement that now was assumed to lie below 1 km -1500 m depth.

abstract: Following the first public announcement on 18/11/1976 by Western Mining Corp. of its giant Olympic Dam copper, gold and uranium discovery on Roxby Downs Station, Newmont Pty Ltd began a detailed assessment of the Stuart Shelf region of South Australia. Although the latter company did not yet know the nature of the mineralisation or controlling host strata at Olympic Dam, it swiftly made application to the SA Department of Mines for the grant of exploration licences over available ground located north-west of Olympic Dam, selecting areas occupying a trend that lay to the east of the Torrens Hinge Zone (THZ). The subject Margaret Creek area was chosen because it covered coincident broad regional gravity and magnetic anomalies that are situated close to the intersection of an east-northeast trending geophysical lineament and the THZ. Newmont entered into a 50:50 joint venture partnership with BHP subsidiary Dampier Mining Co. early in 1977, and EL 335 was granted to both companies in the middle of that year along with six other Exploration Licences covering adjoining ground in the Anna Creek - Mount Woods region which looked to have a similar geophysical character, and which lay over a linear crustal feature that appeared to link major copper deposits further south (Olympic Dam, Mount Gunson and Moonta-Wallaroo). Within the Newmont-Dampier exploration project area, the target sought was of Olympic Dam type, i.e. large tonnage, low grade primary Cu-U mineralisation occurring in or near to a crystalline basement host.  Initial field activities commenced in August 1977, with the acquisition of detailed ground magnetic and gravity surveys over regional geophysical anomalies, which in the case of EL 335 comprised the One Tree Bore and Mount Morgan gravity anomalies. Prospect grids were surveyed there and reconnaissance hand-held magnetometer readings were taken at 250 m intervals along principal traverses. Solo Geophysics were contracted during September 1977 to take gravity readings at 250 m x 2500 m station spacing over both anomalies (99 readings on each grid respectively). On each grid, a preferred drill site for conducting a stratigraphic test was picked by Newmont's chief geophysicist.  Drilling was begun in mid-October 1977, when vertical rotary mud precollared and then NQ/BQ diamond cored stratigraphic/exploratory hole SR6 was taken to 550.0 m total depth on the Mount Morgan anomaly, reaching TD on 31/3/1978. This hole ended within the Tapley Hill Formation, having passed through a thick section of Upper Adelaidean strata only thinly covered by Mesozoic to Recent sediments. No significant mineralisation was encountered. There were indications of oil shale horizons in the Mesozoic cover sequence.  Heavy rains that occurred for the rest of 1978 delayed progress on vertical hole SR8 at the One Tree Bore anomaly, which had been rotary mud precollared to 100.6 m depth late in 1977.  During 1978, Newmont carried out office-based regional basin studies to inform its stratabound, African Copperbelt style epigenetic mineralisation model. Using stratigraphic data from water wells and other boreholes, thickness estimates were made for the local Recent to Palaeozoic cover sediments. An in-house study of 1:100,000 scale aerial photomosaics and Landsat images was performed to map lineaments over a wide prospective belt running northward along the Torrens Hinge Zone from Moonta to the northern end of the Stuart Range Project acreage, and the aforementioned prominent NNW-trending lineament was clearly identified. The intersecting pattern of lesser lineaments observed around Mount Gunson and Olympic Dam appeared to be repeated along strike on the eastern side of EL 335.  Early in November 1978, drillhole SR17/2 was begun at Joe's magnetic anomaly, a large feature which extends from the eastern side of EL 335 onto the JV's adjoining EL 441. This hole was percussion precollared to 200 m before being continued with HQ/NQ/BQ diamond coring until drilling was suspended at 934.8 m depth, close to the capacity of the rig then in use. This same rig was then shifted onto previous hole SR6 and was used to deepen it from 550 m to 889.55 m depth by April 1979, when the drilling here was also suspended. At this stage, both of the cored holes still remained within Adelaidean glacial sediments. During November 1978, gridding and the acquisition of ground magnetic and gravity survey data were undertaken at the small Turret gravity anomaly located 10 km north of Joe's Dam (85 gravity stations read at 250 m x 2000 m precision).  During the first half of 1979, Newmont assessed the results so far obtained from its two deep diamond cored holes at Margaret Creek, and compared the stratigraphy that it had encountered there against the newly revealed type of cover rocks from the Roxby Downs Station region that it was able to log during an inspection it made of WMC's drillcore from the RD16 hole recently put in at Olympic Dam. This work showed the company that it must continue drilling much deeper on its own ground to penetrate below the Adelaidean sedimentary sequence and reach prospective basement, and that it would need to develop a conceptual tool for evaluating structural and geophysical anomalies prior to doing deep drilling. Therefore Newmont immediately made plans to conduct seismic reflection surveys on its project licences, particularly on the Margaret Creek licence once it was renewed for a second term. At a meeting of the three JV partners held in June, it was further resolved to deepen hole SR17/2 at Joe's anomaly to a depth of 1400 m. Following both of these costly decisions, which it did not support, BHP elected to withdraw from the joint venture. Also during this period, the groundwater outflows from certain artesian mound springs which lie within the EL 335 area were geochemically sampled for dissolved pathfinder elements which might point to the proximity of target mineralisation, but no significant assay values were obtained.

abstract: As part of an ongoing multi-licence programme of exploration for Roxby Downs / Olympic Dam style copper-gold-uranium [IOCG-U] mineralisation that might exist along the eastern margin of the Stuart Shelf, the licensees took up the Strangways Springs area in mid-May 1979.  Initial work comprised making a review of available drillhole information and preparing to conduct surface-based geophysical and geochemical surveys. But subsequently, when the JV partners conducted some deep stratigraphic drilling and seismic reflection surveying a short distance to the south-west on their adjoining Mount Morgan EL 335, this work indicated that, there in general, >1500-2000 m thickness of Adelaidean metasediments could overlie the prospective Middle to Lower Proterozoic crystalline basement rocks. Accordingly it was concluded that possibly an even greater thickness of such cover might be expected to be present on the subject EL 475, where no clear geophysical evidence of the presence of upfaulted basement blocks could be seen, because this area lay further to the east or Adelaide Geosyncline depositional side of the location drilled by DDH SR 17/2. Thus it was now considered that the economic viability of locating any Olympic Dam type target mineralisation in this area had become much downgraded.  In terms of new field work undertaken by the JV, the groundwater outflow from certain artesian mound springs which lie within the EL 475 area was geochemically sampled for dissolved pathfinder elements which might point to the proximity of target mineralisation, but no significant assay values were obtained.

abstract: Ongoing exploration undertaken in the Stuart Shelf area extending north-westerly from Stuart Creek to the vicinity of William Creek, Coward and Strangways Springs, for Olympic Dam type mineralisation, was based on lineament studies and interpretation of regional and detailed gravity and magnetic surveys.  Continued diamond core drilling at the second of two selected gravity/magnetic targets (Joe's anomaly), has extended stratigraphic and exploratory drillhole SR17/2 from a depth of 934.8 m to TD 1500 m, which was attained on 19/11/1979, but the hole remained within a section of Sturtian glacial sediments and failed to penetrate to the base of the Adelaidean sequence. No evidence of proximity to underlying basement was detected in the drill core. Several zones of weak hematisation were logged in the newly drilled stratigraphic section, but no significant sulphide occurrences were seen, and core samples taken for assay at regular intervals failed to return any trace metal values of interest. It was concluded that the target pre-Adelaidean basement rocks are here too deeply buried to be of metalliferous ore interest. No geological material was encountered by the drilling which would explain the cause of the large magnetic anomaly.  An exploratory 12-fold seismic reflection survey of 3.5 line km run over three short traverses at the northern end of Joe's aeromagnetic anomaly, undertaken for the joint venture partners by contractor SADM in the vicinity of hole SR17/2 during 4-14th September 1979, failed to locate the top of the pre-Adelaidean basement. Preliminary interpretations suggest that this contact may lie at >2000 m depth below the surface, or that the acoustic impedance contrast of the rocks on either side of the top of basement unconformity is very subtle. name: mesac6339
title: Cadaree Hill (part of the Stuart Range Joint Venture Project). Progress reports and final report to licence expiry/full surrender, for the period 11/8/1977 to 10/8/1978.
notes:
Geographic Locality: Stuart Range;Cadaree Hill;Aimee Creek;Nilpinna Station;Anna Creek Station;1977 Cadaree Hill Gravity Survey
Doc No: Env 03091
Drillhole: Willow bore;SR14;(140841);SR14/2;(140842)
abstract: Following the first public announcement on 18/11/1976 by Western Mining Corp. of its giant Olympic Dam copper, gold and uranium discovery on Roxby Downs Station, Newmont Pty Ltd began a detailed assessment of the Stuart Shelf region of South Australia. Although the latter company did not yet know the nature of the mineralisation or controlling host strata at Olympic Dam, it swiftly made application to the SA Department of Mines for the grant of exploration licences over available ground located north-west of Olympic Dam, selecting areas occupying a trend that lay to the east of the Torrens Hinge Zone (THZ). The subject Cadaree Hill area was chosen because it covers a coincident gravity-magnetic anomaly that is situated west of the THZ on an east-northeast trending ERTS lineament. Newmont entered into a 50:50 joint venture partnership with BHP subsidiary Dampier Mining Co. early in 1977, and EL 340 was granted to both companies in the latter part of that year as an addition to six other Exploration Licences covering adjoining ground in the Anna Creek - Mount Woods region which looked to have a similar geophysical character, and which lay over a linear crustal feature that appeared to link major copper deposits further south (Olympic Dam, Mount Gunson and Moonta-Wallaroo). Within the Newmont-Dampier exploration project area, the target sought was of Olympic Dam type, i.e. large tonnage, low grade primary Cu-U mineralisation occurring in or near to a crystalline basement host.  Initial field activities commenced in September 1977, with the pegging of a prospect reconnaissance grid consisting of three 8 km long lines spaced 2.5 km apart. Ground magnetic survey readings were made at 250 m intervals along the grid traverses, followed by a gravity survey of 99 stations read at 250 m intervals. The data from these surveys were interpreted and a preferred drill site was picked by Newmont's chief geophysicist for conducting an initial stratigraphic test. The intent was to drill to 350-400 m depth to try to penetrate possible Upper Proterozoic strata, i.e. metasediments or granitic breccias, that might contain geochemical vectors to mineralisation.  Drilling began during November 1977, when hole SR14 was vertically rotary mud precollared to 194.9 m depth, being stopped within a silty and carbonaceous mudstone of the upper Permian sequence when available casing for the hole was all in use. Deeper continuation of this hole by diamond coring was not subsequently undertaken, however, after the JV's ensuing assessment of Pexa Oil's earlier (1970) seismic and gravity survey data recorded for the Cadaree Hill prospect region led them to make a much revised and now unfavourable estimate of the likely depth to basement there (>900 m). Hand-held scintillometer scans of the recovered drill cuttings from SR14 gave very low radioactivity responses (1-2 counts per second combined U/Th).  Because hole SR14 had intersected some drill cuttings fragments of Permian brown coal over the depth intervals 93.8-103.0 m and 125.8-134.9 m, it was later decided to follow-up that occurrence by redrilling the site and coring through those equivalent intervals. During June-July 1978, twinned vertical hole SR14/2 was rotary precollared to 81.0 m and then NQ diamond core drilled to TD 145.0 m, from a collar position located 30 m to the south-west of SR14. However, the single 1.67 m thick brown coal intercept which was made in SR14/2 between 129.08-130.75 m core depth was not considered adequately prospective to cause the JV to want to retain EL 340, so licence tenure was allowed to lapse at the end of Year 1.  Hand-held scintillometer scans of the recovered drill core from SR14/2 gave very low radioactivity responses (2-3 counts per second combined U/Th). A single, 1 kg bulk sample of sawn half-core from the Cadaree Hill coal seam was laboratory tested by proximate analysis for BHP, and the results are appended to the licence final report. Newmont's project engineer later performed an indicative economic assessment of the occurrence's marketability for electrical power generation, versus consideration of comparable factors relating to existing brown coal supplies to SA. The Cadaree Hill coal appeared to be of better quality than what was currently being mined at Leigh Creek, but there were too many other discouraging factors to overcome to contemplate undertaking its development, even should the seam be proven to both thicken and occur more shallowly in the area.

[Palynology of Kennecott] DDH Warriner Creek 1 (Delhi Petroleum Pty Ltd palynological laboratory report 404/1).   8 drill core samples from DDH Warriner Creek 1, originally drilled under tenure of EL 345 (Mount Purvis) by Kennecott Explorations, were assessed for their palynostratigraphical position, hydrocarbon source rock potential, and organic matter maturity. Samples from the Early Permian Stuart Range Formation have a fair source potential. Only 4 samples from this interval yielded identifiable microspores. All other samples were barren. An unconformity between the Stuart Range Formation and the glacial Boorthanna Formation is inferred. Kerogen analysis data, and a range chart of palynomorph taxa identified, are included, the former perhaps representing some of the best potential oil source rocks seen to date in the Early Permian of SA.

abstract: In an ongoing search for possible buried Olympic Dam type stratiform copper-uranium deposits in the Mount Purvis area, which were expected to occur within the basal Adelaidean metasedimentary sequence, a stratigraphic diamond drillhole was put down to 464 m total depth on a selected, 300 gamma intensity  magnetic anomaly defined by new, detailed airborne surveying.  Prior to this test drilling, Adelaidean strata were unknown either in outcrop or in the subsurface across the north-western Stuart Shelf.  Associated with a regional gravity spot 'high', the magnetic anomaly was presumed to relate to a 500-600 m deep subsurface source in the form of a local basic intrusive body either emplaced at the Carpentarian basement surface or existing 'blind' within it. The vertical drillhole (DDH Warriner Creek 1) penetrated pre-Adelaidean gneisses at 413 m depth beneath a Mesozoic and Permian sedimentary section, but the target Adelaidean sequence was absent, thus significantly downgrading this particular area's potential.  It appears that north of latitude 29 degrees 40 minutes South, Adelaidean sediments may be absent over most of the Stuart Shelf, or lie below economic depth limits in the most easterly part.

abstract: As part of a regional search for possible buried Olympic Dam type base metal mineralisation, one vertical percussion hole was drilled to 200 m total depth at a site located 9.5 km NNW of Parakylia Homestead, principally to gather stratigraphic information, the plan being to attempt to penetrate basement, and also to intersect the base of the Tapley Hill Formation, if present.  The drillhole passed through the expected Cretaceous - Cambrian - Adelaidean cover sequence, but was ended prematurely above the Tapley Hill Adelaidean target due to high groundwater influx from the vuggy lowermost Cambrian section into the uncased lower part of the hole. The drillhole was geochemically sampled, radiometrically logged for total count gamma radiation, and one groundwater sample was tested for total dissolved salts. No anomalous metal assays were returned. No further drilling was attempted on EL 358 pending receipt of results from Seltrust's concurrent other stratigraphic/exploratory drilling being conducted on nearby Portulacca Ridge EL 291 lying to the east. When those results were to hand it was decided that the local depth to basement is probably in excess of 500 m, and this, coupled with an apparent lack of prospective gravity or magnetic anomalies within the licence area, prompted a decision to surrender tenure.

abstract: Exploration for possible Olympic Dam type mineralisation in an area located 20 km south-west of William Creek has consisted of grid-based ground gravity and magnetic surveys followed by the drilling of a deep diamond exploratory / stratigraphic hole (SR13/2, TD 900.27 m) to test pre-Adelaidean basement beneath the Anna Creek gravity anomaly.  This anomaly was regarded as prospective because it occurs adjacent to a NNW-trending regional tectonic lineament that parallels another to the east which passes through the Moonta-Wallaroo, Mount Gunson and newly discovered world-class Olympic Dam copper deposits. No significant metalliferous mineralisation was encountered in the drillhole, but other stratigraphic drilling conducted to the south by this joint venture, who presently hold 9 ELs in the region, plus inspection of the Western Mining Corp. RD-16 drill core from Roxby Downs, has led to a clearer understanding of Stuart Shelf basement / sedimentary cover relationships and probable ore host rock intrusive / hydrothermal settings, and has confirmed the need to drill into the pre-Adelaidean basement to reach Olympic Dam type targets. A geochemical survey of groundwater precipitates from actively flowing artesian mound springs which are located within EL 341 was also undertaken, with analyses performed for Cu, Mo, U and F, but no anomalous values were returned.

title: Bute. Data release at the full surrender of a subsequent licence : Progress reports to licence expiry/renewal, for the period 10/6/1978 to 28/9/1979.
notes:

abstract: As part of ongoing base metal exploration of the area surrounding Bute, initial work done after the expiry of EL 248 comprised the completion of one diamond drillhole to TD 411.2 m within Carpentarian basement, targeting a magnetic anomaly thought to originate at the base of the Adelaidean Tapley Hill Formation, above an interpreted unconformity with the Emeroo Quartzite, for inferred Myall Creek / Mount Gunson type copper mineralisation. The drillhole was unsuccessful, and this exploration strategy was then abandoned in favour of seeking more easily accessible, possible near-surface Mississippi Valley type base metal deposits in Cambrian carbonate sediments that outcrop and subcrop in much of the region.  The new exploration model adopted by NBH involved reliance on geochemical and IP methods to disclose possible stratabound base metal MVT mineralisation. Following on from preliminary 1:50,000 scale geological mapping to establish likely Cambrian basin boundaries, regional reconnaissance and infill auger geochemical drilling (1022 holes for a total penetration of 8836.2 m, along traverses with holes spaced at from 200 m down to 10 m spacing) and detailed IP surveying of resultant anomalies (23.7 lime km of profiles having a 50 m electrode spacing) were performed to outline prospects with known lead-zinc anomalism in Lower Cambrian dolomitic rocks.  Two such prospects, Wehr's and McPherson's, showed early promise, but the IP work later carried out at McPherson's showed that the polarisation anomaly there was caused by graphitic and pyritic Tapley Hill Formation shale rather than Cambrian rocks containing base metal sulphides. However, at Wehr's prospect located 3.5 km north of Bute, minor indications of stratabound lead and zinc mineralisation were detected in the northern part of the IP anomaly, when auger bedrock geochemical high values of 18,500 ppm Pb, 9000 ppm Zn and 2300 ppm Cu were borne out by an air hammer drillhole maximum Pb value of 5000 ppm returned from within a silty dolomite unit in the Winulta Formation.  As part of follow-up deeper geochemical testing of all identified Cambrian prospects by air hammer percussion drilling (104 holes for 2625.1 m), further drilling at Wehr's returned a best mineralised intercept of 1.5 m @ 1.5% Pb, where the zone of mineralisation apparently plunges to the south-east and diminishes to nought at depth. Orientation mercury sampling of the soil profile above the Wehr's mineral occurrence returned a highest value of only 47 ppb Hg, which bears out the probable limited size of the mineralised zone.

abstract: A subtle regional gravity high located 10 km east of Uro Bluff on the eastern margin of the Stuart Shelf was the subject of further investigation by a new group of licensees seeking buried Olympic Dam type mineralisation.  After a consultant's review and re-interpretation of the Western Mining Corp. geophysical data, it was decided to run a detailed gravity survey over the anomaly to better define its features.  64 gravity stations were read in a 7 square km area above the anomaly peak, with additional ground magnetic, ground radiometric and track etch survey coverage being obtained to supplement the gravity readings.  No anomalous results were seen by the latter methods, while the actual gravity anomaly was replicated in a slightly different shape, but no more convincingly than the original, and is still centred 2 km north-west of Baker Dam.  It was concluded that the weak gravity response represents a minor perturbation that forms part of a larger positive regional high, and that it probably lacks a significant, dense metalliferous source.

abstract: To determine whether the subject licence could contain geophysical or geochemical anomalies that might reflect Olympic Dam type copper-uranium mineralisation potential within the Precambrian basement rocks, consultant Ian Youles designed a programme comprising a gravity survey and drilling, to define and investigate the peak of the broad regional gravity high recognised within the EL. Following a literature study of the characteristics of Stuart Shelf and Olympic Dam economic geology, a 25 square km prospect area was investigated, on a 400 m x 800 m grid, with track etch, gravity, ground magnetic and ground radiometric surveys. The resultant gravity data had a total range of about 2 mGal, and revealed a central low but no highs. The magnetic data indicated a high in the north-western corner of the grid, but this does not coincide with any other geophysical feature. Radiometric and track etch data revealed no significant radiation variations. The potential for discovering Olympic Dam style mineralisation is therefore now considered as low. Limited scout drilling for sedimentary uranium in basal Tertiary sediments may be warranted, but achieving drilling rig access through the prevalent dunes would be expensive.

abstract: Stratigraphic diamond drillhole WWD1, which had been percussion precollared to a depth of 72.2 m, was completed on 13/6/1978 at a total depth of 762.1 m, and was ended within probable Mount Bayley Range Siltstone Member of the Brachina Formation, after it had drilled through probable Bunyeroo Formation and ABC Range Quartzite. WMC considered that the depth to pre-Adelaidean basement in the West Well prospect area is likely to be very great if a complete remaining section of Brachina Formation is present there.  No exploration was conducted on EL 404 between July 1978 and August 1979.  After BP had farmed into the Stuart Shelf Project in July 1979, WMC flew a low level airborne magnetic/radiometric survey across the project licences. In the channel area located between Andamooka Island and the mainland to the west, a number of uranium channel anomalies were evident on the airborne scintillometer records, and these were field checked by the company. The radioactivity appeared to emanate from ferruginous fracture fillings in the Arcoona Quartzite. Previously, some detailed investigations had been done here by Mines Administration on its SML 623 [see Env 1789], which had suggested that the radioactivity is due to uranium daughter elements. WMC decided to further analyse the surface occurrences of radioactivity, and the results obtained indicated concentrations of up to 16% Mn and 22 ppm U in the fractures. Gamma ray spectral scans that WMC made on the fracture fill material showed that the radiation is due to uranium daughter isotopes, principally Pb-214 and Bi-214, supported by Ra-226. The two samples tested gave 390x and 490x normal equilibrium levels of Ra-226 activity. Instrumental delayed neutron activation analysis of the same samples yielded uranium concentrations of 3.6 ppm U and 20.2 ppm U respectively.  Ground geophysical surveys which had been scheduled to take place after September 1978 on the surface of Lake Torrens immediately east of Andamooka Island had to be postponed for sixteen months due to adverse conditions for access onto the lake caused by continual wet weather. However, by January 1981 this work was able to be completed over the Torrens, Island Dam and Willaroo Lagoon grids. After the resulting gravity and magnetic data were interpreted and drilling sites chosen, more stratigraphic diamond drilling began and was in progress on the Island Dam prospect at the date of surrender of EL 681. Here drillhole IDD1 was at an interim depth of 541 m, after reaching the basement unconformity at 349 m depth. Within the basement, minor chalcopyrite is present in sheared and altered felsic ?volcanic rocks, in association with haematite, magnetite and pyrite.

abstract: In WMC's continuing exploration of the area surrounding Arcoona Homestead and its underlying regional gravity structure, the completion of ground geophysical surveying has confirmed that closed magnetic highs exist at both Pearson Hill and Cocky Swamp; importantly, the Cocky Swamp anomaly has an associated gravity high, so it will probably be given priority for drilling. However, subsequent re-levelling of the grids at both prospects, using a newly available digital quartz pressure transducer, revealed that positive residual gravity features are present at each locality. During February 1979 an alternative drilling proposal was generated by the WMC geophysicists, to drill a stratigraphic test hole 8.5 km to the south-west of Arcoona Homestead at the Winjabbie Dam West prospect, where the interpretation of a new ground magnetic survey had produced a top of basement depth estimate of only about 300 m, versus 1000 m interpreted at the same time for the newly profiled Horse Well aeromagnetic anomaly. A precollar percussion drillhole was completed to 300 m at Winjabbie Dam West during April 1979, and the test was continued with diamond coring during September-November 1979 down to an interim total depth of 867.6 m, at which point the installed rig capacity was exhausted. Pre-Adelaidean basement was penetrated at 827.2 m depth, and drilling was stopped in ?banded iron formation containing veins and disseminations of chalcopyrite and bornite, which lies beneath a sequence of felsic volcanic tuffs and breccias. The drill core from the bottomhole 5.4 m thick interval below 861.6 m when assayed averaged 0.54% Cu, including 1 m @ 2.0% Cu, besides containing an average of 7 ppm U3O8. Early in 1980, a more powerful diamond rig was brought onto the WJD1 site, and this incomplete stratigraphic hole was deepened and completed at TD 1015 m. The aforesaid zone of copper mineralisation was found to continue deeper, to give a total intersection 61.4 m thick (from 861.6-923.0 m depth) that was shown to contain 0.4% Cu overall. This mineralisation is mainly chalcopyrite, with minor bornite in its upper part, and occurs within banded magnetite-chert-chlorite iron formation. Beneath the mineralised zone, pyrite is the predominant sulphide mineral present.  Between June 1980 and February 1981, much additional drilling was carried out by WMC on its renewed EL 682. A previous drillhole at Oak Dam prospect, AD1, was deepened with the new diamond rig from 510.05 m to a total depth of 823.8 m, while elsewhere several precollar percussion drillholes were completed through the Stuart Shelf cover rocks at the Horse Well, Dromedary Dam, Burden Hill and Coorlay Ridge prospects, and further deep stratigraphic diamond drilling was undertaken at Cocky Swamp, Dromedary Dam and Heaton Hill. The drillhole at Heaton Hill (TD 1186.2 m) reached granitic gneiss basement at 1133 m depth. A notable highlight of the latest drilling was the intersection of significant mineralisation in hole AD1, with 3 m @ 0.63% Cu and 193 ppm U3O8 over the cored depth interval 534-537 m, plus 68 m @ 0.31% Cu and 680 ppm U3O8 from 600-668 m, that includes 10 m @ 0.46% Cu and 3700 ppm U3O8 from 625-635 m. This mineralisation comprises chalcopyrite plus uraninite in part, and occupyies haematitic breccias overlying granitic rocks. Because of this discovery, follow-up diamond drilling on the Oak Dam prospect is currently underway, at hole AD3 sited 1.6 km west of AD1. It is also now proposed to drill test the previously overlooked eastern gravity high of the Arcoona gravity structure.

name: mesac18545
title: Geology of the Stuart Creek - Charlie Swamp area, northern South Australia.
notes:
Geographic Locality: Southern Stuart Range;Stuart Creek;Charlie Swamp;Coorichina Dam;Pidleeomina Dam;Lake Pidleeomina;Cockatoo Cliff;Split Hill;Arthur Fault
Doc No: Env 03463
abstract: As a B.Sc. Honours project with the Geology Department of the University of Adelaide, which was sponsored by the South Australian Department of Mines and Energy, the author during 1978 carried out geological mapping of a nearly 400 square km area surrounding Charlie Swamp.  This locality lies 20 km north-east of the Stuart Creek Opal Field, which in turn is 60 km north of Andamooka.  In addition, an investigation of the nature of the Marree Formation, in particular its coarse clastic content, was undertaken in the diggings at Stuart Creek.  87 backhoe trenches were opened and examined, while several hundred samples were collected from the trenches and adjacent outcrop for later laboratory study, to supplement field notes. In the Charlie swamp area, Mesozoic sedimentation commenced with the "Stuart Creek Beds", a transgressional unit of fine sand infilling depressions in the pre-Mesozoic topography.  The overlying Marree Formation, of Early Cretaceous age, comprises a marine sequence of mud with sandy conglomeratic interbeds and "erratics".  Much of the coarse material has been transported by shore-ice rafting.  A major conglomerate bed, closely parallelled by the base of a bleached profile, extends over a distance of 80 km. Following a period of deep weathering, silicification and erosion, the ?Middle Tertiary Mount Sarah Sandstone, a fluviatile-lacustrine unit of sand and sandy limestone was deposited overlying the Marree Formation. ?Late Tertiary ferruginisation and silicification have produced varicoloured stains and silcrete within the Mount Sarah Sandstone and the Marree Formation. Late Tertiary or Quaternary events include a further bleaching and the formation of red-brown colluvial sediment and development of silcrete and gypcrete.
