abstract: [ Note - here is only Part 1 of an abstract relating to 2 separately indexed parts ].  Exploration carried out over the Peake and Denison Inliers by the joint venturers since mid-2000 has targeted possible large-scale Proterozoic ironstone-hosted Cu-Au deposits within a highly magnetic basement terrain having geophysical features similar in size and intensity to those existing on the Stuart Shelf around the Olympic Dam deposit. At the outset the joint venture partners targeted potential IOCG deposits with attributes akin to Olympic Dam, Ernest Henry and Candelaria, viz. size (>500Mt), grade (>2% Cu equivalent) and depth of cover (<200 m).  Work commenced with a review of all available previous geophysical and drillhole data, the compilation of this data into proprietary systems, and image processing and interpretation of the magnetic and gravity data. Next, four selected coincident or semi-coincident gravity and magnetic anomalies were gridded (340 line km), 26 line km of trial dipole-dipole IP surveying was carried out at three of these prospects, and another 287 line km of exploratory dipole-dipole IP surveying was then done on all four prospects to define drilling targets. Following an interpretation of the IP results, Rio Tinto drilled 6 angled rotary mud/diamond holes during November-December 2000 at the Davenport Creek prospect on Mount Charles EL 2620, to test a narrow, 3.4 km long IP lineament within an elongate, 7 km long coincident gravity/magnetic feature, looking for structurally controlled IOCG mineralisation.  The drillholes were sited along two traverses spaced 3.4 km apart, and comprised totals of 1079.1 m of rotary mud precollars, plus five diamond core tails aggregating 1358 m of basement penetration. The drilling at Davenport Creek showed that a 154-196 m thick veneer of unconsolidated Quaternary and variably indurated Mesozoic Great Artesian Basin sediments unconformably overlies the basement. Multi-element chemical analysis of the drillhole basement core samples gave disappointing results, while geological logging of the drill cores established that the intensely Fe-metasomatised, metasedimentary, metavolcanic (gneiss) and granite rocks encountered by the drilling are non- to weakly copper mineralised, with rare native copper visible in tight, near-vertical fractures (best assays 0.1-0.27% Cu from hole DD00MC003). Drillholes DD00MC001 and 002 met with moderately dipping zones of massive magnetite-actinolite-albite alteration, containing massive coarse magnetite over wide intervals between depths of 163-204 m in hole 001 and 244-402 m in hole 002. The presence of the massive magnetite and of highly variable iron oxide mineralisation is thought to reflect initial high temperature Fe-K alteration, while the presence in the other drillholes of alteration assemblages containing only trace to minor iron plus rare copper sulphides suggests that a later, low to moderate temperature Fe metasomatic event occurred for which the fluids were of low sulphur content. For this drilling target, the observed geophysical response was attributed to a series of metasomatic magnetite (low P) accumulations lacking a significant sulphide overprint. Ground checking of eight total count radiometric anomalies recognised in data from the 1996 airborne survey flown by Renison Gold Corp. over the Spring Hill prospect found that the majority correspond to exposures of Cretaceous Bulldog Shale and artesian mound spring deposits. Two small, unmapped Proterozoic basement inliers were located approximately 7.5 km south-east of Spring Hill, within EL 2620.   The next stage of work, carried out during 2001, comprised detailed geological mapping of structures and alteration exposed in the Peake, Denison, Kingston North and Algebuckina Inliers, concentrating on areas of known mineralisation in order to determine its controls. Two differently-orientated groups of veins associated with different alteration assemblages were identified : the NNW trending haematite and haematite-quartz veins have proximal potash feldspar alteration, whereas the NE striking copper-mineralised quartz-only veins have a chlorite-epidote-magnetite alteration. However, Rio Tinto was unable to find any surface evidence of a large IOCG alteration system. Concurrently collected rock chip samples (58) failed to reveal any new geochemical anomalies. In the sediment-covered region flanking these inliers to the west, aeromagnetic data was used to prioritise areas for conducting gravity surveys aimed at detecting any concealed massive iron-rich alteration within the basement there. A 1 km x 1 km gravity survey of 954 stations covering 1500 square km was completed in July 2001. This disclosed six prospective gravity features, three of which were subsequently chosen as drill targets, after their evaluation with dipole-dipole IP traverses to establish the existence of chargeable and conductive sources that could represent buried sulphides. During September 2001, Rio Tinto drilled 9 angled exploratory RC holes for a total penetration of 908 m at these prospects located within EL 2549 Mount Denison. Two of the drillholes reached Palaeoproterozoic basement, and five others were ended in Neoproterozoic sediments. No significant drill sample assay values were returned, other than some elevated Cu-Au in the Wirriecurrie Granite drilled by holes RC00PS001 and 002 on the Peake Siding prospect, which is a 3 mGal gravity high with a chargeability anomaly on its southern margin. The tenor of the assay results plus the weak haematite alteration implies a distal IOCG mineralising event, which is interpreted to have been focussed at the nearby Peake Ruins. An additional fence of three angled holes (RC01PS003, RC01PS004 and RC01PS005) was drilled to test a robust hargeability feature. RC01PS004 encountered weakly anomalous Zn-Pb-Ag hosted by Neoproterzoic carbonaceous and graphitic siltstones. The northern of two weak chargeability anomalies coinciding with a 2.5 km x 4 km, 6 mGal gravity high at Big Blyth West prospect was tested with one RC drillhole (RC01BB001) to TD 136 m. This hole revealed weak Cu anomalism hosted by shale. A 2 km x 3 km area of elevated gravity and chargeability at Rockwater prospect was tested with one RC drillhole (RC01RW001) to 160 m depth. Nothing of interest eventuated. The gravity anomalies for this western region were considered by Rio Tinto to have been adequately resolved, and no further work there was recommended. Furthermore, the company considered that no immediate opportunities remained within the project licences for it to discover IOCG deposits that would meet its open pit mineable criteria, although it still believed that discoveries might be made of mineralisation that diverged from such constraints. The area of large-scale iron-altered basement in the eastern part of the project acreage remained mostly untested, and thus clearly retained prospectivity for having economic IOCG mineralisation. Therefore Rio Tinto and BHP-Billiton decided to seek a farm-in partner to advance the project aims, who would commercially entertain chasing smaller size targets under increased depth of cover.  For the following 25 months no ground-based exploration was performed, while Rio Tinto reviewed the project prospectivity against its other mineral venture commitments on a global basis, and then successively presented a project farm-out package to various interested parties.

abstract: Exploration for possible buried Olympic Dam style Cu-Au-U-REE deposits in Proterozoic basement on the eastern flanks of the Peake and Denison Ranges, in an area located approximately 65 km south-east of Oodnadatta, has concentrated on a very large Bouguer gravity anomaly (the Toby prospect) lying proximal to the north-eastern margin of the Gawler Craton and to the Torrens Hinge Zone.  Work completed to date has consisted of doing regional prospectivity studies, image interpretation and geophysical modelling of available aeromagnetic and gravity data (which has resolved a number of arcuate basement features suggestive of calderas or volcanogenic collapse structures similar to those inferred for the Stuart Shelf and Katinka prospect areas), and the drilling of a 261 m deep rotary precollar hole for a planned deep test of the Toby prospect.  A 3 m bottomhole core was cut from bedrock in the drillhole, which was later petrographically identified as being an altered massive microdolerite, partly brecciated and with extensive carbonate and smectite alteration. Secondary iron oxide stains and trace small grains of native copper were observed in the drill core sample thin sections, but assays of the rock proved unremarkable.  Licence operator Platsearch then decided not to deepen the hole to the target depth of 600 m by diamond drilling, since the required indications of proximity to an Olympic Dam - type mineralising environment appeared to be absent, and on 8/4/2004 Platsearch transferred its 50% licence interest back to the other licensees.  During the remaining licence period the incumbents have sought to attract a new joint venture partner to fund further drilling at the Toby prospect, and have conducted additional geophysical modelling studies of the target structure aimed at refining the definition of subsidiary gravity anomalies.

abstract: The reports comprising this data release package describe exploration for economic deposits of base and precious metals that have possibly formed within Neoproterozoic metasediments, the underlying Palaeoproterozoic basement, and in Cambrian carbonate rocks present on the north-eastern Stuart Shelf and the Adelaide Geosyncline / Torrens Hinge Zone west of the Willouran Ranges.  The initial work addressed perceived potential for finding Zambian Copperbelt / Mount Isa / Nifty style sedex copper mineralisation, with lesser emphasis given to locating Mississippi Valley /Irish type base metal deposits in limestones, or Beltana type zinc deposits in similar stratigraphic settings, associated with diapiric breccias intruding large structures. Exploration progressively evolved starting with a malachite occurrence in an area known as Airport Claypan, on EL 2340 to the north-east of Lake Torrens. The initial geochemical Mobile Metal Ion (MMI) survey returned encouraging results, and as a consequence the MMI sampling coverage was expanded greatly, following low amplitude magnetic features as a guide to where to conduct the sampling programmes. Many prospects also emerged via other lines of investigation, viz. from the re-analysis of anomalies identified by previous explorers, such as the unresolved gravity anomalies at Clara [St Dora] and Titan, and from the discovery of copper mineralisation at unrecorded old mine workings at Clara and West Mount. Later, most new drilling targets were generated from a coupling of ground gravity survey traverses with follow-up dipole-dipole induced polarisation surveys.  For 2000-2001 (Year 1 of the amalgamated expenditure agreement reporting period for its Lake Torrens Project, having a first anniversary date of 25/5/2001) Tasman Resources reported that it employed a wide range of remote sensing, geochemical and geophysical methods. These include soil MMI and rock chip sample analyses, an interpretation of all available aeromagnetic data, a ground radiometric survey, and an induced polarisation survey. During these 12 months a total of 1,625 geochemical samples, representing 152.2 line km of traverses, were taken from various parts of the project area. The licensee commissioned a detailed report prepared by Archimedes Consulting on magnetic anomalies located within the top 2 km of a large section of the project area. In addition, Tasman Resources participated in a multi-client deep crustal aeromagnetic study conducted by Archimedes Consulting on behalf of various companies and PIRSA, which covered an extensive area of SA and NSW and included the whole of Tasman's tenement acreage. The dipole-dipole complex resistivity induced polarisation surveys carried out by the company comprised a total of five lines with an aggregate length of 13.6 line km, profiling various targets on the project.Tasman also spent much time on negotiating and concluding agreements, pursuant to Part 9B of the Native Title (SA) Act 1994, with registered Native Title claimants for the Lake Torrens region. As part of this stakeholder consultation the company conducted Aboriginal heritage surveys in conjunction with relevant Aboriginal groups, thereby obtaining clearances to enable it to carry out further exploration activity, include drilling, on twelve dispersed target areas.   Following the discovery of the large Prominent Hill deposit by Minotaur Resources in November 2001, Tasman's focus shifted towards identifying drillable iron oxide - associated copper-gold (IOCG) targets in deeper basement, and also any Ernest Henry type copper-uranium-precious metal occurrences within haematite-rich granitic rocks, besides considering the potential for possible nickel-copper-platinoid metal deposits to form in layered mafic intrusions like the Bills Lookout Gabbroic Complex.  Many prospects fitting into one or other of these models emerged from several sources: the re-analysis of anomalies identified by previous explorers, such as the unresolved gravity anomalies of Clara and Titan; the occurrences of old workings as at Clara and West Mount; and the anomalies generated from the Tasman geochemical MMI coverage, in particular Thrust.  Exploration during 2001-2002 extended across the project licences, and included drilling of several geochemical anomalies, some with attractive IP chargeability features, such as indicated at Clara St Dora. Follow-up gravity and IP surveys conducted on several geochemical anomalies advanced certain others to drillable status, including Watermans Plain (M1) prospect in the southern sector of Marathon, the coincident gravity and chargeability highs at Clara, and the gravity high at Titan. With regard to the last-named prospect, Geoscience Australia’s examination of fluid inclusions in drill core from WMC’s 1976 drill hole BD1, in the course of their Gawler Project research, had indicated the presence of copper-bearing hydrothermal fluids in association with magnetite-rich alteration. This drillhole, although weakly mineralised, penetrated part of a hydrothermal system which Geoscience Australia (Skirrow, 2002) believed may have been too hot, at approximately 400-500 degrees C, to permit the precipitation of significant concentrations of copper minerals. By analogy with published studies of Olympic Dam, located some 32 km to the south, which indicated that the copper there was deposited under lower temperature conditions, copper would be expected to have precipitated in the cooler outer parts of the Titan prospect system at temperatures below 350 degrees C. Drawing also from newly acquired knowledge about the Prominent Hill geological setting, Tasman concluded that the peripheral zones of the Titan system required urgent assessment. Tasman's geophysical consultants (Resource Potential, 2002) had noted that the prospect’s magnetic anomaly is displaced some 400 m to 600 m west of the centre of a pronounced gravity anomaly. It was thought that this eccentric relationship could indicate haematitic alteration of the magnetite. Both anomalies overlap, are about 3.5 km long, and are aligned along what is believed to be the controlling structure. This structure, with its inferred intense haematitic alteration, constituted a copper/gold exploration target. The zone of interest occupies a vertical interval of a least 300 m from about 500 m depth, and is about 3 km in length.  During 2002-2003 activities included prospect 1:5000 scale geological mapping, related soil (631 samples) and rock chip (33 samples) analyses, the resampling of stored diamond drill core from Western Mining Corp.'s 941 m deep, 1981 drilled Bopeechee East prospect exploratory hole BD1 to allow making detailed petrographic studies of the basement rocks, 43 line km of dipole-dipole and gradient array IP plus limited trial CSAMT surveying, a downhole IP survey at Clara St Dora, five detailed infill gravity surveys (2455 stations), forward modelling and inversion of gravity and IP data, and a total of 8563.3 m of RC percussion drilling, plus 376 m of diamond NQ2 core drilling, in 84 holes put down on ELs 2543, 2594 and 2772.  Prospects drilled were Clara St Dora, Watermans Plain, Shelf 6, Saddle Hill and Titan. The 6 drillholes at Clara St Dora targeted coincident gravity and IP anomalies thought to reflect sediment hosted base metal mineralisation, but these were shown to arise from interbedded dolomites and pyritic, graphitic shales of the Skillogalee Dolomite. The best mineralised intercept obtained was over the depth interval 306-308 m in hole CRC002, where 300 ppm Cu was returned by laminae and discordant veinlets of magnetite-pyrite-chalcopyrite present in a weakly dolomitic meta-argillite. This mineralisation is thought by Tasman Resources to have formed during greenschist facies regional metamorphism of the original clastic sediments. The company noted that there are some stratigraphic and structural similarities between the geological setting of this mineralisation at Clara St Dora and that at the giant, high grade N'Changa mine of the Zambian Copperbelt.  Gravity and IP anomalies at Shelf 6 were tested for possible MVT style mineralisation with 7 drillholes, and traces of this were met with at the top and bottom unconformities of the Andamooka Limestone and also within it in permeable oolitic facies. Similar targets at Watermans Plain and Saddle Hill were drilled in 13 holes, and iron sulphides were also encountered within the Andamooka Limestone. An attempt to deepen the single hole at Saddle Hill to investigate an IOCG gravity feature revealed by inversion modelling had to be abandoned when the hole trajectory flattened unacceptably. The 6 holes drilled at Titan were designed to test an IOCG system formerly discovered by Western Mining Corp., and to attempt to locate high grade mineralisation within interpreted chargeable, dense but non-magnetic zones believed to represent cooler, more oxidised portions of the system. The drilling encountered extensively magnetite-haematite / pyrite / chalcopyrite -altered ?Palaeoproterozoic basement below 600 m depth.  During the 2003-2004 project reporting year Tasman Resources undertook an intensified round of prospect geophysical surveying, data processing and interpretation, besides carrying out further deep RC and diamond drilling on the Clara St Dora, Titan and Marathon South structures(20 RC holes for 980 m, plus 2483.2 m of rotary precollar/diamond drilling in 3 holes, including 1985.1 m of coring). The geophysical surveys comprised regional (2455 stations) and infill (278 stations) gravity, audio-frequency magnetotelluric (AMT), IP, Mise-a-la-Masse (MALM), and downhole magnetometric resistivity (DHMMR) and transient electromagnetic (DHTEM) methods. Some diamond - seeking exploration was also performed, involving field checks of discrete small magnetic anomalies having the characterisitcs of possible buried kimberlite, plus associated loam heavy mineral sampling to look for kimberlite indicators. All analytical results were negative.  For the 2004-2005 project reporting year, the emphasis was mainly on evaluating existing IOCG prospects, which were further examined through applying new geophysical data processing and modelling techniques, assisted by the collection of petrophysical data from drill cores, plus the drilling of another three deep diamond cored holes at the Marathon South prospect for a total recovery of 2327 m of NQ2 core. Some additional ground reconnaissance over several potential intrusive diamond-bearing magnetic features was performed, but heavy mineral analyses of a composite loam sample taken over a genuine such anomaly on EL 2989 were again found to be negative for kimberlitic indicator minerals. During this year Tasman Resources also undertook trial soil gas sampling for SDP (soil desorption pyrolysis) along the 28 km length of an interpreted north-west striking, north-east dipping basin margin fault zone mapped within ELs 3109 and 3209. The intent was to look for hydrothermal geochemical pointers to possible MVT style, Lennard Shelf (WA) type base metal mineralisation that could have formed within the Cambrian Andamooka Limestone proximal to this fault, perhaps through dewatering of Proterozoic sediments during Delamerian inversion of the basin. 240 soil gas samples were collected at 300 m intervals along 48 fault transects spaced 600 m apart. The nature of the regolith present at the sample sites was also noted. Two coherent anomalies were seen in the SDP results, within a generally anomalous region of sand dunes developed over clay pans, that follow for ~6 km along the strike of the fault.   During 2005-2006 the licensee mainly carried out petrographic studies of drill cores recovered from its four Marathon South drillholes, besides performing shallow RAB drilling at the Thrust prospect (8 holes for a total penetration of 611 m) to test IP and soil geochemical anomalies on ELs 3123 and 3140. The petrographic work identified the basement brecciated lithologies at Marathon South as essentially being hydrothermally disrupted clastic sediments, in contrast to a previous interpretation which had given them a volcaniclastic origin. The new interpretation places the breccias in a similar genetic setting to the brecciated host greywackes found at Prominent Hill. All of the assay results from the RAB drilling were of uniformly low tenor, with base metal values matching those for average Mesozoic shales. The highly anomalous soil geochemistry recorded in the northern Lake Torrens region is therefore attributed to unusual soil enrichment of base metals arising from the lengthy action of significant weathering and erosion on the regolith profile occurring at Thrust. Some weak chargeability features seen in the accompanying IP and CSAMT data for this prospect are now believed to be due to lithological variations within the Brachina Formation, which underlies a much thinned and ferruginised Bulldog Shale. At the end of the reporting period Tasman Resources was probing back down into its previously completed deep open drillholes at Titan and Marathon South, to try to determine their suitability for logging to acquire downhole temperature gradient measurements, with a view to assessing the region's geothermal energy prospectivity. No other work took place on the subject licence areas for the remainder of 2006.

title: Data release [made at SA Director of Mines’ discretion] : Hawks Nest. Annual reports to licence expiry/renewal, for the period 12/3/1999 to 11/3/2004.
notes:
Notes: This release to the public of the subject mineral exploration data, namely, company data which was acquired more than 5 years ago, is being done by DSD in accord with the provisions of Section 77D of the Mining Act 1971 and Regulation 88 of the Mining Regulations 2011.  Hawks Nest Project operator AuIron Energy Limited is the controlling shareholder of SASE Pty Limited, holding 90% of the issued shares. The remaining shareholders in SASE Pty Limited are smelting technology company Ausmelt Limited (5%) and Indonesian steelmaker PT Krakatau Steel (5%). The concept of the Project is to develop a major integrated pig iron smelting and power generation facility utilising the nearby extensive coal reserves held under licence by AuIron, the large resources of iron ore indicated on EL 2587, and the Ausiron smelting technology that has been developed by Ausmelt.  On 10/2/2003, a 12-month duration option and access agreement for EL 2587 was approved by the SA Minister of Mines, allowing Minotaur Resources Ltd and BHP Billiton Minerals Pty Ltd to conduct exploration instead of SASE Pty Ltd. The option holders subsequently withdrew from this agreement on 11/3/2004. BHP Billiton sole funded the IOCG exploration work carried out until the end of April 2003, when the unsuccessful outcome of drilling the Billah prospect became known, after which time Minotaur Resources funded the IOCG drilling at Stafford Swamp and Hallam Rise, and subsequently, gold-only exploration work. abstract: An area comprising two separate sub-blocks centred ~115 km south-southeast of Coober Pedy and located to the west of the Stuart Highway is being explored for Archaean to Palaeoproterozoic banded iron formation iron ore mineralisation of economic grades and quantities that may occur under cover in the near surface bedrock. Known occurrences of iron ore in the Hawks Nest region comprise a cluster of seven prospects within Block “A” of the subject tenement, the Giffen Well prospect within Block “B”, and several occurrences lying outside of the licence to the north-east.  During the initial licence reporting year (1999-2000), no field work was done.  During licence Year 2, AuIron Energy Limited (AuIron), on behalf of its subsidiary SASE Pty Ltd, undertook an iron ore appraisal drilling campaign between March and May 2000 which was designed to upgrade the resource status of two known iron ore occurrences on EL 2587 that had been previously identified by MESA. The intent was to confirm the existence of sufficient iron ore feedstock for the initial 25 years of operation of a commercial 2.5 Mt/year Ausmelt smelter that was planned to be constructed by SASE in the vicinity of the Gina Siding on the Tarcoola - Alice Springs Railway, ~45 km west of Hawk’s Nest. AuIron's reviewing of the MESA drillhole data had suggested that the Kestrel deposit had the highest likelihood, at its current stage of exploration, to provide a large tonnage, long term base load feedstock, whereas the Buzzard deposit could provide higher grade iron ore that was potentially “direct smelting ore” (generally known as DSO). Consequently AuIron completed programmes of infill drilling on both of these targets. A total of 14,914.75 m of drilling (12,284 m of RC and 2,630.75 of diamond coring) was completed. A regional evaluation of the iron ore potential of the rest of EL 2587 was also carried out, based on remote sensing data and the interpretation of regional geophysical data.  During licence Year 3, independent ore reserve consultants Hellman & Schofield Pty Ltd were retained by AuIron to estimate the iron resource grades and volumes for the Kestrel and Buzzard deposits based on all available drilling data. At a 30% Fe cutoff grade, to 135 m below surface, Kestrel was calculated to contain total Measured, Indicated and Inferred Mineral Resources of 220 Mt @ 36% Fe. At a 55% Fe cutoff grade, to 125 m below surface, Buzzard was calculated to contain total Measured, Indicated and Inferred Mineral Resources of 6.7 Mt @ 60% Fe. With the objective of identifying any further higher grade haematite targets analogous to Buzzard, a detailed gravity survey of 2268 stations was undertaken at Hawks Nest in October-November 2000, on a grid aligned along a prominent gravity linear defined in previous data. Gravity stations for this survey were read at 25 m intervals along twenty-eight x 2 km long lines spaced 200 m apart. Dr Rod Eddies of Earth Solutions was retained by AuIron to perform an interpretative review of the results from this survey, as well as to undertake the reprocessing of and a re-interpretation for open file magnetic and gravity datasets derived from surveys previously carried in the same area by MESA. Metallurgical testing of the Hawks Nest magnetite ore was begun under the direction of consultants Promet Engineers Pty Ltd. Stage 1 investigations performed by Amdel examined the effects of different ore head material grind size on magnetite recovery through a magnetic separator, using four typical drill core samples. In May 2001, a first partial relinquishment of EL 2587 was made by SASE, when it became reduced in area by 573 square km or ~25.2% of the originally granted size, through dropping tenure of five separate peripheral parts of both licence sub-blocks. These were portions of ground showing low magnetic and gravity relief in the regional geophysical data, which had been taken to indicate either: a) that thick cover sedimentary sequences of Cretaceous or Quaternary age blanket the basement in these areas, and hence, should iron mineralisation be present, it would be difficult to detect and most likely uneconomic to mine; or alternatively, b) the basement metamorphic rocks contain low amounts of high density and/or magnetic iron - containing minerals.  During licence Years 4 and 5 [reported together in early 2004], Minotaur Resources was the operator for all exploration activities while the option (to purchase the tenement) was in force. Finding possible shallowly buried IOCG type massive sulphide mineralisation was the main objective of the work undertaken after February 2003. Minotaur had earlier contracted geophysicist Chris Moore to perform 2D and 3D inversion modelling of the 15 mGal amplitude main gravity anomaly at Hawks Nest, and in January 2003 he reported that he had identified some possible shallow source dense bodies as suggested drill targets. Petrophysical property measurements (141 readings), petrological examinations (5) and assaying (5) were done on selected BIF core samples from stored historical CRAE drillhole DD88HN1 early in 2003. In March 2003, part of a detailed ground gravity survey, with a coverage subset comprising a total of 330 stations, was read over three small separate grids located adjacent to and south of the Bulgunnia Shear Zone, at either 1 km x 500 m or 500 m x 250 m station spacings. The grids were located south-west of Hawks Nest and between 10 and 13 km away from there, within the Black Oak paddock of The Twins Station. In April 2003, three semi-coincident gravity/magnetic anomalies as defined by the detailed gravity data were tested by drilling 3 vertical RC holes for 777 m. 45 basement drill cuttings samples were assayed for gold and base metals. The source of the Billah anomaly was not explained by the rocks encountered there, but magnetite-haematite BIF units with up to 40% Fe content which were penetrated at Stafford Swamp and Hallam Rise did explain those gravity and magnetic anomalies. However, since no evidence of IOCG type rock alteration was seen, it was decided that no more work was warranted. Shortly afterwards, BHP Billiton chose to cease participation in the option and access agreement for EL 2587.  Because Minotaur was aware that previous exploratory RC drillholes within the Hawks Nest region had revealed widespread gold anomalism within basement lithologies which is closely associated with iron-rich rock types (e.g. in hole HKN99, 4 m @ 4.3 g/t Au, and in hole HKN53, 4 m @ 0.59 g/t Au), the company acting alone in May-June 2003 undertook an initial reconnaissance soil calcrete geochemical sampling programme comprising 194 samples to infill places previously not so sampled, and to follow up anomalies generated from earlier auger sampling. The gold-in-calcrete assay results upgraded one of those earlier gold anomalies, and also delineated a separate broad regional anomaly requiring further follow-up. So next, 105 infill calcrete samples were collected within the latter anomaly, which showed that it is less coherent than was expected and had now 'dissolved' to only contain a few much smaller spot high gold value clusters, thereby lowering its prospectivity. Nevertheless, in December 2003, Minotaur decided that it would test the three largest of the regional infill sampling spot gold-in-calcrete highs by drilling 49 vertical aircore holes for 837.9 m along seven traverses. Covered bedrock lithologies ranged from weathered ?Bulldog Shale, or weathered older saprolite, to granitic rocks having minor sericite alteration. Disappointingly, only minor copper and gold values were returned from assaying 309 drill cuttings samples. After this, Minotaur chose not to exercise the licence purchase option, and withdrew its participation.  On 8/4/2004, tenure of a much reduced (by 1217 square km or ~73.6%) area of the licence (still in the form of two separate sub-blocks) was renewed by SASE Pty Ltd for a second five-year term, as EL 3196.  All of the ground deemed not to be highly prospective for magnetite BIF was dropped, as three large portions.

title: Tregalana. Data release made in lieu of submitting a licence first partial surrender report: annual reports for the period 22/2/2001 to 21/2/2005.

abstract: Exploration of an area located 30 km south-west of Port Augusta initially sought possible Olympic Dam style iron oxide-hosted copper-gold deposits within concealed Mesoproterozoic basement, plus Mount Gunson style stratabound copper in the overlying Adelaidean strata.  The latter objective has local substance in the form of the buried Myall Creek copper sulphide occurrence discovered in 1975 by Australian Selection Pty Ltd, which comprises interbeds of sandstone and dolomitic shale containing sub-economic copper (+ minor lead-zinc) mineralisation that is covering an area of about 3 km x 15 km at the base of the Adelaidean Tapley Hill Formation.  Merritt Mining in 1998 concluded that the Myall Creek mineralisation is probably an epigenetic deposit derived from a nearby basement source, perhaps by leakage upwards along basement-penetrating faults.  That company also identified mineralised pebbles in Backy Point Beds underlying the Tapley Hill Formation.  These appeared to be eroded from a nearby basement source. After an initial geophysical assessment involving the merging and re-processing of existing airborne magnetic survey data, a ground gravity survey was conducted by EL 2800 licensee Minex in the Myall Creek vicinity during late November 2001 (208 stations at 1 km x 2 km spacing along 7 N-S lines) to help define structural lineaments interpreted from the aeromagnetic data, and to model possible dense basement targets for epithermal mineralisation.  The survey results disclosed a NW-SE trending gravity ridge within the interpreted deep graben of Adelaidean sediments that underlies the Myall Creek prospect.  A regional licence joint venture was entered into with Eagle Bay Resources NL on 15/11/2002, to progress exploration both on Tregalana and the adjoining Cultana tenement to the east.  In December 2002 Eagle Bay performed a detail infill ground gravity survey at Myall Creek (677 stations on 19 E-W lines for a 500 m x 125 m station spacing), which resolved the gravity ridge anomaly into a more deep-seated source lying to the north-west, and a shallower one in the south-east.  A consultant's 3-D inversion modelling of the gravity and magnetic data suggested that the latter anomaly could lie at a depth of about 205 m below surface, and was thus feasible to drill.  A single RC/diamond drillhole was put down to 354 m total depth in May 2003 to test this gravity feature to see if it was the older primary basement source for, in particular, the "pebble" copper mineralisation found at Myall Creek.  However, hole TR7 encountered, beneath minor Recent sediments, only an un-mineralised sequence of Tregolana Shale Member, Whyalla Sandstone Member, Brighton Limestone Member, Tapley Hill Formation, Beda Volcanics and Backy Point Beds, and the inferred up-faulted Mesoproterozoic basement was not reached.  Eagle Bay has since concluded that the gravity high probably reflects uplifted Beda Volcanics in a narrow northwest-trending horst formed by post - Adelaidean faulting. Because the postulated presence of IOCG mineralisation in the local basement is still unproven, further gravity and drilling work similar to that already completed is now being planned, to try to address the potential of the remaining licence portion and that of the associated Cultana tenement.

abstract: Olympic Dam style copper-gold mineralisation was the target of exploration in an area which lies about 100 km north-east of Port Augusta, and adjacent to south-eastern Lake Torrens.  All of the available aeromagnetic data for this area were re-processed and re-interpreted, resulting in the definition of several anomalous features which were investigated by detailed ground gravity surveys.  The results suggest that most magnetic anomalies are due to linear, dyke-like features, while several anomalies have been interpreted as being of possible volcanic origin.  These latter anomalies require further modelling to provide follow-up drilling targets.  A preliminary 12 drilling targets have been selected, where holes are planned to reach a total depth of 350 m to investigate the basement geology and provide samples for testing to allow calibration of the geophysical models.

title: Lake Torrens Station and Hawker West (the Torrens Project). Joint annual reports, plus separate final reports to licences' respective full surrender, for the period 30/4/2003 to 1/6/2010.
notes:
Notes: Continuation of tenure of the EL 3081 subject area by the same company principal from his former EL 2860 (see related reports held separately in Env 9878).  On 1/2/2007, a new publically listed company, Empire Resources, acquired Torrens Resources and took over ownership of EL 3081. Empire had previously taken up a contiguous licence, EL 3530, and thenceforth reported in a joint way about the work done on both of these tenements. EL 3530 was surrendered on 22/10/2009, and tenure of EL 4152 was allowed to lapse on 1/6/2010.
Geographic Locality: South-eastern Lake Torrens Plains;Mount Eyre;Cotabena;Bald Hill;Willochra Creek;1995 SAEI Area B15 Aerial Magnetic Survey;2002 Lake Torrens Gravity Survey;2004 Lake Torrens Gravity Survey;2007 Lake Torrens Gravity Survey

abstract: Olympic Dam style copper-gold mineralisation was the target of exploration in two adjoining areas which lie about 100 km north-northeast of Port Augusta and 55 km west of Hawker, on alluvial plains adjacent to south-eastern Lake Torrens.  All of the available regional aeromagnetic data for these areas were re-processed and re-interpreted, resulting in the definition of several anomalous features which were then investigated by conducting detailed ground gravity surveys. The results suggested that most discrete magnetic anomalies are due to linear, dyke-like features, although some anomalies were interpreted as being of possible volcanic origin. The underlying geological terrane was thought to consist of an early Adelaidean / Carpentarian sedimentary succession and/or Lower Proterozoic basement. The basement rocks were thought to belong to the Stuart Shelf Domain. This interpretation was based solely on the magnetic and gravity character of the project areas studied. Interpretation of the regional geophysical data identified a pattern of buried structural features that is characterised by strong block faulting, and this geometry is believed to be similar to that of structures found in IOCG prospective areas located north-west and north-northwest of Lake Torrens. Modelling of the blind magnetic features on the project licences undertaken by geophysical consultants produced estimated shallowest source depths in the range of 150-300 m. The nearest drillhole control lay at least 7 km away to the south-east.  Further (to those completed previously within EL 2860) small, detailed ground gravity surveys were acquired on EL 3081 by Torrens Resources during 2002 and 2004, which resulted in the delineation of at least two prospective gravity ridges running alongside magnetic highs. One of these was considered to have spatial similarities to the geophysical signature of the recently discovered Prominent Hill IOCG deposit. Soil geochemical sampling was done at eight sample points across one of the interpreted most shallowly-sourced gravity anomalies. These samples were analysed for 40 elements, but the results were inconclusive.  After a lengthy review of the merged new and old gravity data, and the acquisition in February 2007 by Empire Resources of infill gravity coverage in two priority areas (totalling 1170 stations read on 200 m x 200 m and 500 m x 500 m grids respectively), five preliminary drill sites were selected and given Aboriginal Heritage clearances in September 2007 after inspection and assessment by local Native Title claimant representatives. During October-November 2007, a single rotary mud precollared diamond  exploratory and stratigraphic hole was drilled to a total depth of 770 m to test a gravity anomaly in the centre of EL 3081. This drillhole had to be abandoned due to technical difficulties before reaching its objective. It was found that the sedimentary sequence persisted much deeper than had been prognosed by geophysics, and no Adelaidean or basement rocks were penetrated. Because of the lack of mineralisation seen in the recovered drill core, no downhole samples were submitted for assaying.   Because of the disappointing results from the limited drilling, no other field work took place on the subject licences until the time they were surrendered. A review of the gravity targets was done in 2008, and an unsuccessful attempt made to attract a joint venture to help fund further drilling.

abstract: An area located 30 km west of Pimba, and situated on the eastern margin of the Gawler Craton, was considered to have potential for Olympic Dam style Cu-Au mineralisation, and possibly for stratabound Cu sulphide mineralisation as occurs at Mount Gunson.  Work undertaken consisted of researching and reviewing historic exploration results, and the interpretation of available magnetic, gravity and geological data.  Logs from drillholes that had been drilled within 80 km of the licence showed a best stratabound mineralised intersection of 13 m at 0.36% Zn and 0.11% Pb, from 63 m depth, whilst from the geophysics the regional depth to basement was interpreted to be in excess of 600 m.

abstract: Two areas which lie adjacent to and are situated respectively south and north from Olympic Dam, are considered very prospective for iron-oxide copper-gold (IOCG) mineralisation of Olympic Dam style.  While historic drilling intercepts have shown that the top of basement here lies at between 750-1000 m depth, a re-evaluation of open file geophysical data has highlighted several untested gravity anomalies associated with magnetic complexes.  Infill 1 km x 1 km gravity surveys were run over these anomalies, which, after data modelling, have identified three high priority targets for drilling, as well as numerous lower priority targets.  No significant gravity anomalies, however, were identified in the relinquished areas.

abstract: Exploration for possible economic deposits of buried, Mesoproterozoic basement-hosted IOCG-U style mineralisation is being conducted over two separate multiple-block licence areas in the Olympic Dam district, EL 2931 (Acropolis South) and EL 2932 (North Roxby). The inferred high prospectivity of several significant gravity anomalies located within these tenements was tempered by the high likelihood that for each the depth to basement, as indicated by sparse previous drilling and by geophysical interpretations, would be in the range of ~600-750 m to well in excess of 1 km.  During Year 1 of tenure, licensee Minotaur undertook an extensive data compilation, acquired infill 1 km x 1 km spaced gravity readings over a number of significant gravity anomalies that it recognised in past regional gravity coverage, and commenced a search for a joint venture partner to help fund deep drill tests. The company's re-evaluation of open file geophysical data had highlighted several untested gravity anomalies associated with magnetic complexes, and modelling of the new gravity data combined wth the old clearly identified three high priority targets for drilling, as well as numerous lower priority targets. The high priority targets were Acropolis West (EL 2931: source depth 480 m), Wirrda Well South (EL 2931: source depth 800 m) and Bopeechee West (EL 2932: source depth 700 m).  During Licence Year 2, attempts were made to find a partner to help fund immediate drilling of the high priority targets. However, joint venture negotiations entered into with BHP Billiton and Cogema proved unsuccessful. Minotaur then commenced investigating additional mineralisation models for the greater Olympic Dam area, particularly focussing on models for uranium deposits, as the uranium price had continued to strengthen from approximately US$8/lb U3O8 in 2001 to greater than US$20/lb U3O8 in mid/late 2004. One of the models favoured was for possible palaeochannel sediment-hosted uranium that might have formed at the base of the Pandurra Formation. Minotaur made an assessment of the viability of using shallow seismic surveys as a direct targeting method for this type of deposit setting.  During licence Year 3 of both tenements, gravity surveys were conducted during November–December 2005, achieving complete regional scale gravity data coverage of both tenements. A total of 325 gravity stations were read on EL 2931 and 539 gravity stations on EL 2932, along 33 lines aligned predominantly on a 1 km x 1 km grid. The three high priority IOCG-U drill targets previously identified were further delineated, and their descriptions are as follows:  - The main gravity high at the Acropolis prospect (located just east of EL 2931) has an amplitude of 22 mGal; this large anomaly extends westwards onto EL 2931, though becoming reduced in amplitude, away from a regional airborne magnetic high into a zone of magnetic quiescence. The western margin of the Acropolis prospect is probably controlled by a major NW-trending fault (probable extension of the Andamooka Fault) delineating the western extent of the prominent positive airborne magnetic anomaly and part (but significantly not all) of the prominent regional gravity anomaly. The 8 km x 7 km western portion of this gravity anomaly (here termed the Westopolis prospect) still has a significant amplitude (7 mGal), and despite its modelled ~1.1 km  source depth it is of considerable interest to potentially host haematite-rich IOCG-style mineralisation.  - A small ~2 mGal gravity anomaly (here named Northopolis prospect) on the northern flank of the broad Westopolis gravity anomaly is modelled as having a density of 2.9–3.5 g/cc, source depth of 600–700 m and width of 800–1200 m; these features are entirely consistent with an IOCG-style mineralised breccia pipe.  - On EL 2932, a positive regional gravity anomaly, ~10 km across and with an amplitude of 5 mGal, is probably derived from a body at a depth of ~800 m with a density of 2.83 g/cc. The modelled low density suggests that this anomaly is probably caused by shallower basement rather than by significant density variations within basement lithologies.  Work area Aboriginal heritage clearance surveys over part of the Acropolis South licence area were undertaken in May 2007 and January 2008 by representative Barngarla Native Title claimants, in conjunction with specialist consultants Philip Fitzpatrick and Vivienne Woods. Proposed drillsites and related access ways were cleared, allowing for the commencement of drilling at AS07D01, located 9 km north-west of Roxby Downs Homestead, and at AS08D02, located 2 km west of Bullers Dam, as exploratory diamond coreholes to test the two gravity targets, “Westopolis” and “Northopolis” respectively.  Drilling of AS07D01 commenced at the end of August 2007, and the first stage, consisting of a 210 m vertical RC precollar and subsequent HQ/NQ diamond drilling, was completed by Tom Browne Drilling Services Pty Ltd to a depth of 1410.7 m by mid-September. The Westopolis target gravity source prognosis had suggested that crystalline basement was likely to be reached at a depth of around 800 m, but at the limit of rig capacity, when the hole had to be  terminated, it still remained within Mesoproterozoic Pandurra Formation. Downhole gamma ray geophysical logging was undertaken by Borehole Wireline Pty Ltd on 12/9/2007. The logging truck was equipped with a 1 km long spool of wireline, so this limited the total depth able to be logged to 1000 m. A small gamma ray anomaly was associated with the top of the Pandurra Formation, immediately below the unconformity (379.5 m depth) with the overlying Tregolana Formation. A peak radiation value of 302 cps was recorded at a depth of 381.1 m. Following the completion of the first stage of drilling, interpretation of some newly acquired MT data (see below) suggested that the unconformity with crystalline basement was likely to lie very close to the current termination depth. This interpretation was tested in January 2008, when Boart Longyear used a UDR1200 drilling rig to extend the AS07D01 hole to a new total depth of 1559 m. Crystalline basement, comprising Gawler Range Volcanics (GRV), was penetrated at 1461.9 m depth. Petrological examination of 12 selected basement drill core samples was undertaken by Pontifex and Associates. A Niton portable XRF spectrochamical analysis instrument was used to scan all of the AS07D01 drillcore. 17 elements returned assay values of interest. Uranium anomalism was found to occur just below the unconformity at the top of the Pandurra Formation, with a peak value of 651.72 ppm U at 379.6 m depth. Copper anomalism was found associated with visible chalcopyrite logged within haematite breccia zones present in the basement (peak value 3.16% Cu at 1481.2 m depth). Sporadic anomalous lead values occur in both cover and basement rocks; a peak value of 542 ppm Pb coincides with the peak copper value mentioned above. Three intervals of the cored Pandurra Formation, namely, 880 to 940 m, 1080 to 1170 m, and 1400 to 1410 m, were cut, sampled (quarter core, one metre intervals) and assayed for a broad range of 36 elements by ICP-AES and ICP-MS methods. The laboratory assay results were generally of a low tenor, with the exception of one isolated high copper value of 941 ppm Cu recorded at 1142- 1143 m depth. Following the completion of the extension drilling of AS07D01, drill cores covering the base of the Pandurra Formation and the entire basement interval were also cut (quarter core) and laboratory assayed. The haematite breccia intervals within the GRV basement were found to be associated with anomalous values for a variety of elements including copper, uranium, lead and rare earths, particularly lanthanum and cerium.  Drilling of AS08D02 commenced in January 2008 immediately after the completion of AS07D01, using the same Boart Longyear UDR1200 drilling rig. The hole was precollared to a depth of 21 m using a tri-cone roller bit, and then was extended by vertical HQ/NQ diamond drilling to a total depth of 1487.1 m. It intersected a cover rock sequence similar to that encountered in AS07D01, with one notable difference, which was that just over 200 m thickness of Tapley Hill Formation was intersected above the Pandurra Formation; this unit is not present in AS07D01. Furthermore, AS08D02 intersected only 600 m thickness of Pandurra Formation, compared with the 1080 m intersected in AS07D01. Crystalline basement in AS08D02 was intersected at 1312.0 m depth, which is 150 m shallower than in AS07D01. A Niton portable XRF spectrochamical analysis instrument was used to scan all of the AS08D02 drillcore. Within the cover sequence, sporadic narrow zones having anomalous geochemical values were returned for a number of elements, with several of these anomalies (Cu, Mn, Pb, Zn, U) being coincident with the unconformity between the base of the Tapley Hill and the underlying Pandurra at 710.5 m depth. Scanning of the basement GRV core interval returned only a few isolated higher base metal values (maximum 669 ppm Zn at 1484 m depth).  During October-November 2007 and February-March 2008, Quantec Geoscience were contracted to conduct magnetotelluric surveys at Acropolis South and North Roxby. A total of 46 tensor format MT soundings were collected at 500 m intervals along a single 23 km long line at Acropolis South on renewed EL 3762, and 95 similar format soundings were collected along two orthogonal lines at North Roxby EL 3761 over 46 line km. The purpose of these surveys was twofold, firstly to map the depth to basement with respect to effectively exploring for IOCG mineralisation, and secondly to identify any potential conductors within the basement units. Examination of the 2D inversion of the single line of MT data at Acropolis South showed that the resistivity data can be used to effectively map the depth of basement and also the thickness of the various layers within the cover sequence. Both the 1D and 2D inversions showed a decrease in basement depth going southwards from station 122, from 1400 m to 800 m. Notably, there did not appear to be any increase in conductivity associated with the haematitic volcanic breccia unit, and no other significant conductive responses were seen within the interpreted basement. Analysis of the petrophysical property data collected from lithological unit drill core samples taken in hole AS07D01 showed that there is very little difference in resistivity, density and magnetic susceptibility between the overburden and the basement units. This observation therefore implies that MT, magnetic and gravity techniques are all poorly suited to resolving the depth of basement. The deepest basement sample tested (#8) was slightly denser with an SG of 2.8 g/cc, however, the density difference compared to the overburden SG of 0.13 g/cc is not enough to permit the gravity method to accurately resolve the depth to basement when its upper boundary lies at great depth. At North Roxby, interpretation of the MT data for north-south aligned Line 5 suggested a depth to basement in the order of 800 to 1200 m. A single, weakly conductive basement feature was seen in the northern part of the line, that correlates with a magnetic and 1VD gravity anomaly. It was surmised that this feature may indicate the presence of haematite alteration, albeit at a depth of 1 km. Interpretation of the MT data from east-west aligned Line 6 indicated a shallower basement at the western end of the line, at a depth of approximately 600 m. This deepens going eastwards from station 614, to an interpreted depth of 3 km. At the eastern end of this line, a thicker section of conductive overburden overlies what are thought to be several basement conductors. The lack of variation in density of the basement units in comparison with that of the overburden at Acropolis South may explain the lack of correlation between the two MT line datasets obtained at North Roxby. The variation in gravity response seen along a profile matching MT Line 6, which is at odds to the deepening trend of the MT resistivity data, may be reflecting deeper features than those present in the upper basement section.  Late in 2008,  a study was made of the rare earth elements (REE) present within haematite-rich alteration of typical IOCG-style that is developed within the felsic volcanic rocks cored by hole AS07D01. The investigation involved petrology and routine laboratory geochemical analysis, along with QEMSCAN analysis. 32 drill core samples that had previously been taken from the depth interval 1461.7–1491 m were re-assayed at ALS Chemex, this time using the multi-element mass spectrographic method to determine the concentrations of lanthanum, cerium and other REEs that are often indicative of Mesoproterozoic IOCG-style alteration on the Gawler Craton. The abundances of REEs within AS07D01 were found to be very high, with maximum values of 2920 ppm for La and 4490 ppm for Ce. Highly anomalous zones closely correspond with zones of haematite-rich alteration having iron concentrations of 40–50% Fe2O3. The correlation is especially evident for core depth intervals 1471–1473 m and 1477–1478 m, but other slightly deeper zones of haematite alteration at 1480–1481 m and 1483–1485 m lack REE enrichment. The two REE and haematite-rich core samples at 1471.5 and 1477.1 m were sent to Amdel for analysis by the QEMSCAN® technique, which scans a polished rock section to a resolution of 10 ?m and based upon reflectance spectral peaks then quantifies mineral abundances, mineral associations and grain sizes along with REE phase characterisation. This work revealed that the dominant mineral phases present are haematite (63–71%) and earthy haematite (21–27%), with intermixed minor quartz (2–6%), muscovite (0.2–4%), Ce+La phosphate (0.3–3%) and chalcopyrite (0.1–0.2%). The La+Ce bearing phosphate mineral may be either Ce-rhabdophane or Ce-monazite. During June 2008, photomicrography work was performed on five of the AS07D01 basement drill core samples in order to highlight various distinctive and unusual mineragraphic textures. Of particular interest were classic crystal growth quench textures observed within the petrographic thin sections cut from haematite-rich samples at 1473.5 m and 1477.95 m depth. The haematite in these exists commonly as martite relics after magnetite, and occurs in a variety of microcrystalline forms that include decussate, micaceous and skeletal, along with loosely packed aggregates. These textures are indicative of the quenching of iron-rich fluids or magma from which the primary magnetite precipitated.  Because official Commonwealth Government landowner permission to conduct exploration activities on those portions of EL 3761 and EL 3762 lying within the Woomera Prohibited Area had been rescinded early in 2009, no further work could be done near the Westopolis gravity anomaly and drill hole AS07D01 whilst those access issues remained unresolved. Instead, the JV's exploration activities became focussed on the eastern portion of EL 3762, which is outside of the Woomera Prohibited Area and lies to the south and south-east of Wirrda Well. During October 2008, a gravity survey was conducted over a broad gravity high in this eastern portion of EL 3762, when 350 stations were read on a 500 m x 500 m irregular grid plus 100 m spaced stations two along detailed N-S and E-W traverses, to improve the resolution of existing gravity data. Interpreted in combination with MT survey data acquired during May 2008, when soundings were collected at 29 stations at 500 m spacing along a single east-west line, defining a coincident conductive basement zone, the gravity survey data delineated a regional positive Bouguer anomaly (Aphrodite prospect) with perceived potential for IOCG-style mineralisation, that lies at the junction of two gravity high trends. The peak of the surveyed gravity anomaly at Aphrodite has no associated positive magnetic anomaly, instead being located on a NW-orientated magnetic low which may reflect haematite alteration of the basement. Interpretation of the MT data suggested a depth of basement in the order of 400–800 m and also showed the presence of a single, moderately conductive layer response, potentially bounded by faults, at a depth of ~1 km.  During January 2009 Minotaur, along with joint venture partner Japan Oil, Gas and Metals National Corporation, undertook a single hole drilling programme to test the nature of basement lithologies causing the 2 mGal, 4 km x 1.5 km residual gravity anomaly at Aphrodite. AS09D03 was vertically RC precollared to 245.7 m depth, and then was HQ/NQ diamond cored to a total depth of 804.5 m. Basement was reached at 671.2 m depth, beneath the Neoproterozoic Tapley Hill Formation. The predominant basement lithology encountered consists of a variably foliated megacrystic granitic gneiss (assigned to the Mesoproterozoic Donington Granitoid Suite) which is not sufficiently dense to account for the targeted gravity anomaly. Some pervasive sericitic and moderate red-rock haematitc IOCG-style alteration is present, especially near a number of thin brecciated shear zones, accompanied by a number of thin, brecciated haematite veins plus some minor, late stage chalcopyrite/chalcocite/bornite-bearing carbonate veins. Mafic igneous dykes occurring at depths of 754.1–761.9 m and 758.87–761.9 m were assigned stratigraphically to the Mesoproterozoic Tournefort Dyke Swarm. Within the AS09D03 drillcore, the levels of copper, lead and zinc, as determined by NITON portable XRF spectrochemical analysis scans, are uniformly low for all lithologies. Drill core samples from six selected intervals within the basement were submitted for laboratory assaying of 36 elements via aqua regia digest and emission spectroscopy, but no significant results were returned. The highest copper values obtained, 1020 ppm and 1950 ppm Cu respectively, correspond to veined intervals in the core where there is visible mineralisation. Downhole gamma ray wireline logging of the hole AS09D03 carried out by Toro Energy in January 2009 showed that no radioactive intervals exist within the near-surface Tregolana Shale sedimentary cover sequence, but due to technical difficulties, no gamma ray log data were obtained for the basement rocks units (because all the log data recorded from below 350 m hole depth was lost due to a partly corrupted LAS computer file, but this mishap was not discovered until after the logging unit had been demobilised; a second attempt to log the hole made one month later was stopped by running into collapsed ground at 130 m depth).  The petrological and other information revealed by the drilling of AS09D03 gave the EL 3762 JV partners good encouragement to believe that an IOCG-mineralised system might exist on or near the Aphrodite prospect. Therefore it was recommended that further infill gravity data be acquired to better define the gravity anomaly and to look for evidence of any variations in basement lithologies, prior to re-assessing targets for further drill testing.

abstract: Olympic Dam or Moonta-Wallaroo style concealed iron-oxide copper-gold mineralisation hosted in Palaeoproterozoic and Mesoproterozoic basement rocks of the Stuart Shelf, and Mount Gunson type younger Neoproterozoic sediment-hosted buried copper mineralisation, were the targets of exploration in four contiguous areas stretching from just north-west of Port Augusta, northwards along the southern and western sides of Lake Torrens, to the vicinity of Andamooka.  A review of historic drillhole data and interpretation of new and historic geophysical datasets was followed by acquisition of detailed gravity surveys and by limited first-pass MMI calcrete and soil geochemical sampling over coincident gravity and magnetic anomalies. During October-November 2002, contractor Daishsat Geodetic Surveyors acquired seven small gravity surveys (total 1312 stations) read at densities varying from 2 km x 2 km to 1 km x 500 m. The soil sample analyses undertaken by partial leach and enzyme leach trace metal extraction methods revealed several anomalous partial leach Au and Cu values that were believed to be related to possible deeply buried (>400 m) basement sources, most probably granite intrusions. Large, coincident, water soluble Cu-U-REE surface anomalies were identified at Myall Hill, Crystal Dam, Shore Hill, Pernatty, Whittata and Reordan. The Shore Hill anomaly appeared to overlie a regional gravity anomaly, but infill gravity and surface sampling will be required to better define this prospect. The Pernatty anomaly is located along a north-west trending structure at the base of Corraberra Sandstone outcrop. Several Au-Cu-REE anomalies were observed at Reordan, along the edge of the Pandurra Formation. Calcrete sampling performed over coincident gravity and magnetic anomalies at Illeroo on a first pass 1 km x 400 m grid, closing to 400 m x 50 m, identified several coherent > 3 ppb Au gold-in-calcrete anomalies extending for more than 2 km within an area of 12 km x 2.6 km, that show a pattern similar to calcrete gold anomalism present at other Gawler Craton gold deposits such as Barns and Tunkillia. A peak value of 12 ppb Au was recorded near North Four Mile Dam. However, additional calcrete sampling done at high value sites within Illeroo, plus initial follow-up RAB and aircore drilling (69 holes for a total penetration of 1164 m) at the Homestead anomaly during October 2003, failed to substantiate the previously indicated tenor of gold mineralisation. The best drill intercept made in the bedrock was a disappointing 2 m @ 7 ppb Au from 20 m depth in hole ILA37. This drillhole was ended in fresh dolerite, probably of the Gairdner Dyke Swarm. It is thought that potential remains at Illeroo for finding gold mineralisation in basement rocks beneath the Gawler Range Volcanics, analogous to the situation existing at Roopena.  Planned infill soil sampling and gravity surveying over the geochemical anomalies, to prioritize a selection of drilling targets, did not eventuate before ground tenure was surrendered or allowed to lapse. A search for a joint venture partner proved fruitless, and therefore no work of any consequence occurred after late 2003.

name: mesac26995
title: Data release - as updated : Crystal Brook and Port Pirie (the Wandearah Project). Joint annual reports to licences' respective full surrenders, for the period 2/8/2008 to 26/4/2018.
notes:
Notes: This release to the public of the subject mineral exploration data, namely, company data which was acquired more than 5 years ago, is being done by DMITRE in accord with the provisions of Section 77D of the Mining Act 1971 and Regulation 88 of the Mining Regulations 2011.
Geographic Locality: Mid-North;Crystal Brook;Lower Broughton [River];Wandearah West;Keans Farm;Redhill;Port Pirie;2008 Wandearah Project [Detail] Gravity Survey
Doc No: Env 10146
Drillhole: WDD002;(348139)
abstract: Buried basement-hosted iron oxide - associated copper-gold (IOCG) mineralisation of either Moonta-Wallaroo or Olympic Dam style is the target of ongoing exploration on the two adjacent subject tenements. In addition, the current holder considers that the tenements are prospective for uranium, iron ore and potentially a number of other commodities, targets for which will be addressed as geological understanding progresses with the building of knowledge from regional exploration programs.  Following finalisation of the transfer of ownership of the project licences from Avoca Resources to Rex Minerals ("Rex") in May 2008, exploration activities undertaken by Rex during the 2008-2009 reporting year were as follows:  - A geological review of the project was completed in early 2008. The review was predominantly focussed on evaluation of currently available gravity and magnetic data covering the licence areas, and this led to planning of an infill ground-based gravity survey designed to further define the structural characteristics of the main regional gravity anomaly.  - A detailed ground gravity survey was acquired during September-October 2008, when 1329 stations were read at a nominal 200 m x 200 m grid spacing, infilling the previous gravity data collected at 400m  x 400 m by Avoca. Minor areas of the former coverage were omitted due to landholder concerns about possible crop damage. Following the completion of data processing, interpretation of several offset gravity and magnetic anomalies so surveyed delineated eight targets of interest for drill testing, lying along two elongate gravity anomalies striking in NW and NNW directions.  - Initial exploratory RC precollared diamond drilling was performed by Rex over the period 18th November to 5th December 2008, when a single vertical HQ/NQ cored hole, WDD002, was completed to TD 707.5 m to test a site on the NNW trending structure. The hole intersected a sequence of flat lying dolomitic carbonaceous sediments containing minor chalcopyrite–pyrite mineralisation from 130 m to 190 m depth, before passing into a thick sequence of Corunna Conglomerate and haematitic sandstone continuing to 465 m depth.  From there to 707.5 m depth, the hole encountered basement (Wandearah Formation) comprising pink to green–brown haematitic metasiltstones containing minor brecciation, haematite veining and possible granitic (?Hiltaba Suite equivalent) intrusions. Very minor alteration was noted in this basement section. The drillhole was cased off to allow downhole geophysical logging to be completed at a later date. Visible occurrences of copper mineralisation within the cover sequences, along with geological evidence of a large IOCG mineralising system, were regarded by Rex as highly encouraging. Drill core sample assaying of the chalcopyrite-bearing carbonaceous sediments of the Adelaidean Tapley Hill Formation (host to the Mount Gunson copper deposit in SA) returned intercepts of 28 m @ 0.07% Cu from 133 m depth, and 13 m @ 0.03% Cu from 172 m. However, no IOCG - related geochemically anomalous trace metal values were returned from the basement lithologies assayed.  No follow-up new work was completed during the 2009-2010 project year, owing Rex's concentration of its efforts elsewhere, viz. mainly on the Hillside IOCG deposit that it had discovered on central eastern Yorke Peninsula, where a programme of intensive orebody delineation drilling conducted over that period enabled the release of a maiden resource estimate in July 2010. The entire circumstance attached to the making of this management decision is explained in the annual report letter.  During the 2010-2011 project year, Rex’s exploration effort was still directed at evaluating the Hillside copper-gold deposit (cf. the Moonta South Project ELs 3874, 3875 and 4514). Work being done there continued to focus on advancing the orebody towards production, mainly through conducting intensive drilling, with resource estimates and a conceptual mining study progressively released to the market. Consequently, exploration activity on the Wandearah Project was reduced to a minimal level, and no new technical work was completed. For the same overriding reason, no new work was undertaken on the subject two licences over the lengthy succeeding period 2011-2018, firstly while a number of mining feasibility studies involving multidisciplinary research and risk assessment were performed on Hillside that led to the grant of a mining lease there on 16/9/2014 (ML 6438), and later while the company was actively seeking funds to help it develop the deposit.  During 2017, the company withdrew its application for a subsequent licence to EL 5133 Port Pirie, which lapse in tenure was actioned by DPC on 1/8/2017. Subsequently, on 26/4/2018, EL 5883 Crystal Brook was fully surrendered.

abstract: The Mount Gunson Project tenement package is being explored for three separate types of mineralisation: • stratiform copper mineralisation similar to that of the world-class Central African Copper Belt and White Pine deposit in Michigan. This style of mineralisation would be hosted in flat-lying sedimentary units of the Adelaidean sequence, with copper metal being sourced from the underlying Pandurra Formation redbeds or even from zones of extensive alteration and leaching in the pre-Pandurra basement. The deposits at Windabout and at MG 14, hosted in dolomitic black shales of the Tapley Hill Formation in each case, have similarities to this style of mineralisation. The mineralisation mined at the Cattlegrid deposit, while differing in detail from the classic stratiform copper models, probably represents a local variant of this type of deposit, related to a redox boundary and a zone of structural preparation. • base-metal and gold mineralisation within brecciated and altered lithologies in the pre- Pandurra basement, as seen at the world-class Olympic Dam deposit. Variants of this style of mineralisation are seen elsewhere on the Stuart Shelf, and the tectonic and structural setting of the Mount Gunson region is favourable for repetitions of the Olympic Dam setting. • gold mineralisation of any of the types being explored in the central and western Gawler Craton.  No on-ground field work was conducted by the project JV partners anywhere within the four now partially relinquished portions of the subject licences, although these areas have been assessed as part of various desktop reviews and target generation programmes that were undertaken by the partners. Xstrata took over managing the Mount Gunson JV tenure during January 2012.  On 16/6/2014, Noranda Pacific gave notice to Gunson Resources of its intention to withdraw from the Mount Gunson Joint Venture and sell its 51% interest back to Gunson Resources with effect from 14/8/2014. DSD Ministerial consent to the transfer was subsequently granted on 2/10/2014.
