Report on mapping (for EL 6346) of potential magnetite/haematite breccia, major faults and thickness of cover from magnetic data (consultants' report for the Macallum Group). Appendix to EL 6346 first annual report to 20/5/2020. 82 pages, figures, tables.  On 20/10/2020, a transfer of 100% of licence ownership was made from Macallum Group Ltd to Copper Search Australia Pty Ltd.
Geographic Locality: Arcoona Station;Stuart Highway;Pimba;Island Lagoon
Doc No: Env 13264
abstract: An area located immediately south-east of Pimba has been explored for possible shallowly buried IOCG mineralisation, with a focus on the iron ore potential of magnetite/haematite breccias associated with this mineralisation type.  During the first licence year, no field work was done. Activities were confined to desktop studies of available geophysical data, particularly detailed magnetic data. Starting in 2019, the entire licence area was scanned by a consultant geophysicist using innovative magnetic techniques designed to locate potential iron-related breccias for further evaluation. To perform this work, open file aeromagnetic data from SARIG were reprocessed and 3D models of magnetic point data were generated across the area and down to a depth of around 4 km. This model of magnetic susceptibilities was then viewed as a series of vertical slices in various orientations. A total of 27 polygons containing magnetic features tagged as anomalous were snipped from the gridded data and examined in detail. In general, this work was made more difficult by the ubiquitous nature of Neoproterozoic Gairdner Dolerite dykes throughout the Pimba region. Four potential drill targets were identified, with Target 4 scoring a moderately high ranking. This feature is located on the intersection of two intruding dykes. It has a prominent cylindrical shape with a 580 m diameter, is buried under 890 m of cover, and has a source body depth extent exceeding 1400 m. Due to the very poor gravity coverage of the Pimba area, it was recommended that further ground gravity survey data be acquired in order to assist with evaluating potential targets.  During licence Year 2, the geophysical consultants' report was reviewed, and it was concluded that it had failed to highlight any compelling targets on EL 6346. It was thought that the prioritised targets were most likely to represent responses generated from the Gairdner Dolerite dykes. There is also a discouragingly very thick cover sequence (~1 km) lying over the IOCG target Gawler Range Volcanics and older rocks. It was decided not to conduct further exploration, and to allow the licence's tenure to lapse at expiry.

title: EL 6401 - Billa Kalina area. Annual technical reports from 11/09/2019 to full surrender 27/03/2023.
notes:
Notes: Includes:   - February 2020, Mapping potential magnetite/hematite breccia, major faults & thickness of cover from magnetic data over tenements EL 6400 & 6401 Stuart Shelf, South Australia. Report prepared for: Macallum Group Ltd. Archimedes Consulting for Macallum Group. Appx. 1 for annual report to 10th September 2020. Pg. 11-189.
Doc No: Env 13274
Drillhole: BKDDH01-03
abstract: Exploration Licence 6401 lies in northern South Australia around 600km NNW of Adelaide. The town of William Creek lies around 80km north of the tenement. The tenement sits to the east of the Mt Woods Inlier where a large amount of exploration has taken place, while little attention has been paid to the current tenement area. Exploration in the area has commonly targeted copper and gold mineralisation, with diamond and possible IOCG style mineralisation also targeted. The Billa Kalina Project sits between the Stuart Shelf and the exposed portion of the Mt Woods Inlier, with deep Paleozoic and Mesozoic cover of the down warped Boorthanna Trough to the east, becoming shallower to the west.   During the first licence year to 10/09/2020, exploration activities on EL 6401 was focused on geophysical investigation that were aimed at identifying potential IOCG mineralised structures in crystalline basement. A search and compilation of some of the available data from historic exploration on and around EL 6401 was also carried out. Detailed evaluation of 3D magnetic susceptibility data covering all of EL 6401, together with part of the neighbouring lease EL 6400, was undertaken by Adelaide?based consultants Archimedes. The work involved a detailed analysis of possibly anomalous susceptibility responses that were of a non-stratigraphic response. Eleven targets were generated, 5 of which were selected for a future drilling program.  Also included with the remodelling of the aeromagnetic data were structure models generated at various elevations and a 3D model of the top of crystalline basement. A PEPR for the drilling program was submitted to DEM. A heritage visit was conducted on the 10th and 11th of July, with representatives of the Native Title Group – the Arabana People, an anthropologist, and representatives of Copper Search Australia (CSA).  During the second licence reporting year, no new data was generated by Copper Search Ltd, with work restricted to the preparation and planning for a future drilling program, along with a desktop review.   During the third year of reporting, Copper Search undertook a drilling program on the “Wantamaran Creek” Project. Drillhole targeting was based entirely on the report completed by Archimedes Consulting in 2020 investigating anomalous susceptibility responses. Of the 11 targets generated, 3 were drilled (BKDDH01-03), with the 3 rotary mud/diamond tailed holes drilled for a total length of 1062.7 m. All holes encountered difficulties, with large cavaties, lost rods and bits and sinking casings. All holes were reported as having sufficiently tested the targets without results. Magnetic susceptibility measurements were taken for every meter of core and all holes had their lithology logged. Due to the perceived lack of evidence to support the targets generated through the geophysical re-modelling to produce real drill targets, a full review of the tenement was commenced, with the construction of a database of available open file data and modelling of the GCAS data.   During the final reporting year till surrender (27/03/2023), no new data was generated within the licence area, work carried out during the reporting period was focused on ongoing review of existing data.

abstract: 12 square km of ground have recently been relinquished from the northern end of a small licence area centred ~20 km south-east of Woomera. This licence has been taken up because the region is widely regarded by explorers as being prospective for epithermal IOCG mineralisation beneath cover sequences, as well as for unconformity-related Cu-Co deposits within the cover sequences. The recent discovery by BHP at Oak Dam West of high-grade IOCG mineralisation, but at depths below surface of more than 800 m, has given the licensee cause to contemplate the economic implications of finding a similar IOCG occurrence on its tenement.  A decision was made to relinquish the northern end of the original licence area after available factual and interpretive information about the bedrock features there had been obtained and assessed. No drillholes exist there to prove or disprove this inference.

name: mesac29818
title: Novel technologies for [use in] mining and [earth resource] exploration: remote smart sensor deployment for in situ geophysical analysis. Final report, Project ADI RD01-123 [part of Accelerated Discovery Initiative Round 1, 2022].
notes:
Geographic Locality: Southern Stuart Shelf
Doc No: Env 13328
abstract: Nine compact seismic motion recorders and nine co-located ground probe thermocouples have been deployed at various sites near the Carrapateena mine, to test the efficacy of making continuous remote data collection and the reliability of their transmission in real time via satellite link to far-off control and monitoring bases in Adelaide and Melbourne. The data are being shared between the project partners via the Internet-of-Things in a feedback loop which is designed to achieve optimum speeds of modelling and interpretation.  Fleet Space Technologies (FST) successfully developed, deployed, and tested their smart seismometers known as the Geologic Instrument. These devices are described as “smart” for their technological capability to conduct processing at the node reducing output data volume, and then transmitting the packetised data over the air to a ground control station using a low-power wide area network (LPWAN) protocol. Across the duration of the project, nine first and second-version variant Geologic Instruments were successfully deployed at Carrapateena. During their deployment, the Geologic Instruments monitored for active seismic events in the area. In addition, nine Heat Needles originally designed by Hot Dry Rocks (HDR) and manufactured by FST were installed each in conjunction with a Geologic Instrument. Data collected by both instruments were demonstrated to be transmitted wirelessly from each node to the central Portal gateway. Data from the gateway was then transferred to the cloud via satellite backhaul where it could be aggregated and monitored in near-real time. Since the installation of the second-variant Geologic Instruments, a significant volume of seismic and temperature data was obtained from the field over the satellite backhaul. The Geologic Instruments demonstrated the benefits of real-time heat flow and seismic data for mineral exploration. They also indicated promise in being a geophysical sensor that enables real-time passive seismic exploration.

name: mesac29822
title: A new approach to mapping basin architecture using airborne magnetotelluric survey data - the Copper Coast Project trial. Final report, Project ADI RD02-306 [part of Accelerated Discovery Initiative Round 2, 2022].
notes:
Geographic Locality: South Australia;Mid-North;Mambray Creek;Port Germein;Telowie Creek;Southern Flinders Ranges;Mount Remarkable Fault;Melrose;Bangor;Wirrabara;2022 Copper Coast Project MobileMT Aerial MT Survey
Doc No: Env 13329
abstract: IGO Ltd’s (IGO) Copper Coast Project is located along the eastern margin of the Gawler Craton in South Australia, and covers Proterozoic rocks of the Stuart Shelf, Torrens Hinge Zone and Adelaide Rift Complex, which form part of the Adelaide Superbasin. IGO is of the opinion that its Copper Coast Project represents a significant belt-scale opportunity to discover and develop a sediment-hosted copper deposit, like the giant Kamoa - Kakula deposit on the margin of the Central African Copperbelt. Sediment-hosted copper mineralisation occurs when permeable, oxidised (clastic) sediments are overlain by reduced (marine / lacustrine) sediments, and chemical precipitation occurs at the redox boundary between the two. Copper mineralisation (±lead-zinc) within the Adelaide Superbasin is commonly associated with an unconformity at the base of Neoproterozoic sequences where they overlie Mesoproterozoic “red beds” – in particular, where there is significant relief on the palaeo-topographic surface on which the Neoproterozoic sediments were deposited.  It was hoped that the Accelerated Discovery Initiative (ADI) co-funded airborne magnetotelluric (MT) survey which is the subject of this report would address a significant knowledge gap and improve IGO's understanding of the 3D basin architecture, by assisting with mapping the palaeo-topographic surface as well as the distribution, thickness and depth of key lithostratigraphic units and structures within the project area. These key controls would then be used to vector potential locations of sediment-hosted copper mineralisation. The airborne MT survey was also designed to assist with comparison and validation of previous exploration methods utilised by IGO at the Copper Coast Project, to determine the most effective method(s) for use moving forward.  An oblong area running along the range front 25 km north-east of Port Pirie was chosen to trial the acquisition of a high resolution airborne MT dataset. The survey contractor recorded broadband natural electromagnetic fields, the earth’s magnetic field intensity, and EM VLF data using a helicopter-borne proprietary instrumentation system, in daily sorties flown over 15 days during January 2022. Coverage totalled 1245 flight line km, of which 922 line km or 74% yielded usable, cultural noise-free data. The survey flight lines were orientated east-west and spaced 1 km apart. The towed bird maintained a 76 m mean terrain clearance for the EM sensor and 95 m MTC for the magnetometer. Resulting data was provided to IGO as an inverted resistivity block model. A preliminary examination of these data has identified a significant NW-SE trending feature that is likely to have a structural cause.

name: mesac30217
title: Copper Coast. Final report, Project ADI RD02-291 [Accelerated Discovery Initiative Round 2, 2022].
notes: Doc No: Env 13379
abstract: IGO Ltd’s (IGO) Copper Coast Project is located along the eastern margin of the Gawler Craton in South Australia and covers Proterozoic rocks of the Stuart Shelf, Torrens Hinge Zone and Adelaide Rift Complex, which form part of the Adelaide Superbasin. IGO is of the opinion that its Copper Coast Project represents a significant belt-scale opportunity to discover and develop a sediment-hosted copper deposit, like the giant Kamoa-Kakula deposit on the margin of the Central African Copperbelt.  Copper mineralisation (±lead-zinc) within the Adelaide Superbasin is commonly associated with an unconformity at the base of Neoproterozoic sequences where they overlie Mesoproterozoic “red beds” – in particular, where there is significant relief on the palaeo-topographic surface on which the Neoproterozoic sediments were deposited.  It was hoped the Accelerated Discovery Initiative (ADI) co-funded diamond drill program would address a significant knowledge gap by testing the distribution, thickness, and depth of key lithostratigraphic units and structures at a known prospect, currently interpreted to be a marginal basin environment. It was anticipated that understanding prospect scale mineralisation controls might improve and validate the companies understanding effective hydrological / basin architecture at the project scale. The program was also designed to test the hypothesis that basin architecture is too deep to the east of the Copper Coast Project. If disproved, the search space for sediment-hosted copper mineralisation within the Copper Coast project would effectively double.  A total of 4 inclined diamond cored holes for 2730.9 m were drilled (CCDD05 – CCDD08), with the core geotechnically logged and regularly spaced magnetic susceptibility, conductivity, sonic, density, portable XRF (pXRF) and portable spectrometer measurements taken. A total of 395 half core samples were collected and delivered to ALS Global in Perth for analysis. All samples were analysed using the ME-GRA05, ME-MS61r and pXRF-34 analytical suites.  Holes CCD05 – CCD07 intersected (some or all of the holes) A REDOX front at the unconformity between reduced mudstone and oxidised conglomerate which were seen as evidence of permissive stratigraphy, mudstones which were seen as the reduced trap/seal, conglomerate which was seen as a permeable reservoir/aquifer and arenitic sandstones and/or basalts that were seen as a possible source of oxidised fluids.  Copper appears to have precipitated in small, extensional fractures / veins within the mudstone at the REDOX front, although the overall copper load / capacity of the oxidised fluid is in question. CCDD08 intersected deep water marine siltstone and mudstone and displays no indication of oxidised fluid or alteration. Moving forward, finding a mechanism, either structural or stratigraphic, to dramatically increase the permeability of the reduced mudstones / siltstones will be crucial to finding focused economic mineralisation at Copper Coast.

name: mesac30218
title: Pernatty Lagoon. Final report, Project ADI RD02-295 [Accelerated Discovery Initiative Round 2, 2022].
notes:
Doc No: Env 13380
Drillhole: PSDDH01 - PSDDH02;(376694 - 376695)
abstract: This report pertains to the Pernatty C Zambian Copperbelt (ZCB) Project which was partially funded by a $298,500 grant through the State Government’s Accelerated Discovery Initiative (ADI) which aims to make a major contribution to achieving the South Australian Growth Agenda target through supporting the potential discovery of new mineral and groundwater resources.  The Pernatty C ZCB Project (EL6675) is situated within the Olympic Cu-Au Province within the eastern Gawler Craton approximately 40 km south of BHP's Oak Dam West deposit 20 km south-west of OZ Minerals' Carrapateena Mine and directly east of the historic Mt Gunson Copper Province which shows strong alignment with the well-known ZCB deposits.  Cohiba Minerals Ltd is exploring for sedimentary-hosted Cu-Co-Ag mineralisation, similar to the nearby Mt Gunson Cu-Co-Ag deposits. Recent work has shown that there are considerable similarities between the Adelaide Fold Belt (AFB) and the ZCB in terms of the fundamental stratigraphy and the style of basin closure. Using the ZCB model there is strong evidence to suggest that the unconformable contact between the Tapley Hill Formation (Neoproterozoic) and the underlying Pandurra Formation (Mesoproterozoic) is considered to be prospective for Cu-Co-Ag mineralisation based on the ZCB model. In addition, the carbonaceous Tapley Hill Formation shale shows evidence as a strong redox trap for copper, cobalt and silver mineralisation.  Two inclined diamond cored holes (PSDDH01 and PSDDH02) for 2109.3 m were drilled to test for possible ZCB style mineralisation and Iron Oxide – Copper – Gold (IOCG) mineralisation as a secondary target. The drill holes were situated over separate target zones which had been identified from historical geophysical investigations. The drill holes were logged in detail and strip logged for 580 m (PSDDH01) and 590 m (PSDDH02). Core was sampled based on visual determination of mineralisation, with split core samples sent to Australian Laboratory Services (ALS) for a full suite analysis. While the target of high temperature chalcopyrite vein and IOCG related alteration and/or mineralisation was not encountered, significant mineralisation and assay results were obtained from low temperature calcite - sphalerite veins with Zinc-Lead-Silver association. Assay results for include PSDDH01 0.8 m @ 8.6% Zn, 1.9% Pb, 40.1 ppm Ag from 865 m, 2 m @ 1.2% Zn, 0.2% Pb, and 6.5 ppm Ag from 946 m within calcite veins in the Wallaroo Group and 3.8 m @ 3.9% Ag from 223 m in the Tapley Hill Formation Shales. While drillhole PSDDH02 results included 1 m @ 1.06 ppm Ag from 136 m, 2 m @ 4.07 ppm Ag from 236 m from Tapley Hill Formation Shales, and 2.3 m @ 1.97 ppm Ag from 627 m at contact to basement.   The assay results from the Pernatty C drilling program were quite unexpected and did not align with the predicted occurrence of a ZCB style mineralisation or with copper skarn or IOCG system mineralisation within the Wallaroo Group basement. As assaying was restricted to areas where mineralisation was visible, additional core will be assayed to determine if additional significant Zn, Pb and Ag exists within the core and as to whether predictors for mineralisation also exist. It remains for Cohiba to determine what these set of results represent, the drilling to date has not supported the reasonably well held view that this is a Zambian Copperbelt Style environment and neither was there any strong evidence for copper skarn or distal IOCG mineralisation at depth.

name: mesac30418
title: Copper Coast Project - Final Report - Utilising Seismic to Map, Validate and Understand 3D Basin Architecture and Vector Potential Locations of Sediment-hosted Copper Mineralisation ADI RD03-418 [Accelerated Discovery Initiative Round 3, 2023].
notes:
Notes: Includes:    - HiSeis, 4/1/2022. IGO – Copper Coast. Seismic Interpretation Final Report. HiSeis Pty Lts. Appx. 4.
Geographic Locality: Port Germein;Port Pirie;Germein Gorge Road;Collinsfield Road
Doc No: Env 13392
abstract: IGO Ltd’s (IGO) Copper Coast Project is located along the eastern Spencer Gulf and is centred around Port Pirie. It sits along the eastern margin of the Gawler Craton and covers Proterozoic rocks of the Stuart Shelf, Torrens Hinge Zone, and Adelaide Rift Complex, which form part of the Adelaide Superbasin. IGO is of the opinion that its Copper Coast Project represents a significant belt-scale opportunity to discover and develop a sediment-hosted copper deposit, like the giant Kamoa-Kakula deposit on the margin of the Central African Copperbelt. Copper mineralisation (±lead-zinc) within the Adelaide Superbasin is commonly associated with an unconformity at the base of Neoproterozoic sequences where they overlie Mesoproterozoic “red beds” – in particular, where there is significant relief on the palaeo-topographic surface on which the Neoproterozoic sediments were deposited. Sediment-hosted copper mineralisation occurs when permeable, oxidised (clastic) sediments are overlain by reduced (marine / lacustrine) sediments and chemical precipitation occurs at the redox boundary between the two.   IGO believes that understanding 3D basin architecture is key to discovering sediment-hosted copper deposits. It was hoped that the 2D seismic survey that was co-funded through the Accelerated Discovery Initiative (ADI) would address a knowledge gap and improve the companies understanding of the 3D basin architecture by assisting in the mapping of the palaeo-topographic land surface and the distribution and thickness of key lithostratigraphic units in the project area, along with any structures identified. These factors will be used to direct future exploration targets.  HiSeis were contracted by IGO to complete the 2D seismic survey, with 2 traverses completed in August 2022 - one along Germein Gorge Road in the north of the project area, and one along Collinsfield Road in the south of the project area. The survey was designed to traverse interpreted basin edges to gain a regional / project scale understanding of 3D basin architecture and the distribution, thickness, and depth of key lithostratigraphic units and structures. A total of 58.2 line-km was surveyed, with 37.4 line-km completed in the north and 20.8 line-km in the south. Data was acquired using 2 Vibroseis source vehicles, utilising the flip-flop sweep technique, with a nominal source spacing of 20 m and receiver spacing of 10 m.   The 2D seismic survey successfully traversed interpreted basin edges and provided significant insight into the regional / project scale understanding of 3D basin architecture and the distribution, thickness and depth of key lithostratigraphic units and structures.
